default.q.n3-tango-t13-mon3-20.why.0: (a) 落して is the て-form of the transitive verb 「落とす」 (“drop” or “lower”), whereas the sentence uses the particle 「味が」, so it must take the corresponding intransitive verb.
default.q.n3-tango-t13-mon3-20.why.1: (b) 降りて: This is the te-form of 「降りる」 (to get off, to unload), and it does not combine with 「味」.
default.q.n3-tango-t13-mon3-20.why.2: (c) 落ちて: The te-form of the intransitive verb 「落ちる」. The set expression 「味が落ちる」 means “the flavor declines” or “the taste gets worse,” so 「味が落ちてしまった」 is completely correct.
default.q.n3-tango-t13-mon3-20.why.3: (d) 止まって: is the te-form of 「止まる」 (to stop), and is not used to describe a decline in food quality.
default.q.n3-tango-t13-mon3-21.verdict: The correct answer is 2. 話しかけ.
default.q.n3-tango-t13-mon3-21.explanation:
- Sentence translation: A stranger (someone I didn't know) spoke to me in front of the station.
- Vocabulary & kanji readings:
  + 駅前: in front of the station
  + 知らない人: someone unfamiliar, a stranger
  + 話しかける: to speak to someone, start a conversation (a compound verb: 話す + かける). Passive form: 話しかけられる (to be spoken to).
- Illustrative example:
  + 道に迷っていたら、親切な人に話しかけられた。(When I was lost, a kind person spoke to me.)
default.q.n3-tango-t13-mon3-21.why.0: (a) 答え is a form of 「答える」(“to answer”). It does not fit the context because the stranger approaches proactively rather than answering someone’s question.
default.q.n3-tango-t13-mon3-21.why.1: (b) 話しかけ: The stem of the compound verb 「話しかける」 (to start a conversation). In the passive form 「話しかけられた」, it means “was spoken to by a stranger,” which fits the context.
default.q.n3-tango-t13-mon3-21.why.2: (c) 差し上げ is a form of the humble expression 「差し上げる」 (“to give/present”), used for an action performed by oneself for someone else; it is not changed into the passive form in this structure.
default.q.n3-tango-t13-mon3-21.why.3: (d) 拝見 is the humble form of 「見る」(to see or look at). It is not a passive form with 「～られた」and does not fit the meaning.
default.q.n3-tango-t13-mon3-22.verdict: The correct answer is 3. 評判.
default.q.n3-tango-t13-mon3-22.explanation:
- Meaning: He has a bad reputation among his friends.
- Vocabulary:
  + 友だちの間: among friends, between friends
  + 評判: reputation, public opinion, evaluation. Common expressions: 評判がいい (be well regarded) / 評判が悪い (be poorly regarded, have a bad reputation).
- Common collocations:
  + 評判 ＋ がいい／が悪い
  + 人気 ＋ がある／がない (be / not be popular)
  + 価値 ＋ がある／がない／が高い (have / have no / have high value)
- Example:
  + あのレストランは料理はおいしいが、接客の評判が悪い。(That restaurant’s food is delicious, but its customer service has a bad reputation.)
default.q.n3-tango-t13-mon3-22.why.0: (a) 価値: means “value,” commonly used with 「価値がある／ない」 or 「価値が高い」, not 「価値が悪い」.
default.q.n3-tango-t13-mon3-22.why.1: (b) 判定: Means “judgment/determination of a result” in contexts such as sports competitions or medical examinations. It does not combine with 「～が悪い」to describe an opinion between friends.
default.q.n3-tango-t13-mon3-22.why.2: (c) 評判 means “reputation” or “people’s opinion,” forming the fixed expression 「評判が悪い」(have a bad reputation, be poorly regarded), so it is completely correct.
default.q.n3-tango-t13-mon3-22.why.3: (d) 人気: Means “popularity” or “being well-liked” and is commonly used with 「人気がある／ない」 (“to be popular / not to be popular”), not with 「悪い」.
default.q.n3-tango-t13-mon3-23.verdict: The correct answer is 3. 相談.
default.q.n3-tango-t13-mon3-23.explanation:
- Sentence translation: I tried discussing my future plans and asking a senior for advice.
- Vocabulary and kanji:
  + 進路: future path (choosing further education or employment)
  + 先輩: senior, older student or colleague
  + 相談: discussion, consultation, asking for advice. Pattern: [person] に [topic] について相談する.
- Example:
  + 将来のことで悩んでいるなら、両親や先生に相談したほうがいいよ。(If you are worried about your future, you should talk it over with your parents or teacher.)
default.q.n3-tango-t13-mon3-23.why.0: (a) 冗談: means “a joke” and combines with 「冗談を言う」 (to make a joke). It is not used for seriously discussing a future matter with a senior colleague.
default.q.n3-tango-t13-mon3-23.why.1: (b) 感想: means “impressions” or “thoughts,” and commonly occurs with 「感想を述べる／言う」 (to express one's impressions after an experience); it does not go with 「先輩に～する」.
default.q.n3-tango-t13-mon3-23.why.2: (c) 相談: means “to discuss something or seek advice.” The structure 「先輩に相談する」 (to ask a senior colleague for advice) is completely appropriate in meaning and grammar.
default.q.n3-tango-t13-mon3-23.why.3: (d) 判断 means “to make a judgment” or “to form one's own assessment”; it refers to thinking something through and deciding for oneself, not asking someone else for advice.
default.q.n3-tango-t13-mon3-24.verdict: The correct answer is 4. 調節.
default.q.n3-tango-t13-mon3-24.explanation:
- Sentence translation: Use this button to adjust the speaker’s volume.
- Vocabulary and kanji readings:
  + スピーカー: speaker (a device that produces sound)
  + 音量: volume, sound level
  + 調節: adjustment, regulation (often used for adjusting a variable to an appropriate level, such as volume 音量, temperature 温度, or height 高さ)
- Distinction:
  + 調節: adjusting a physical level or condition appropriately (音量を調節する, エアコンの温度を調節する)
  + 調整: adjusting or coordinating a schedule, plan, or relationship (日程を調整する)
- Example:
  + リモコンでエアコンの温度を調節してください。(Please use the remote control to adjust the air conditioner’s temperature.)
default.q.n3-tango-t13-mon3-24.why.0: (a) 調査 means “investigation” or “survey” (collecting data and finding out the truth), so it is not used for adjusting a device's volume.
default.q.n3-tango-t13-mon3-24.why.1: (b) 検査 means “inspection” or “examination” (such as a medical checkup or product inspection); it is not used for changing the volume.
default.q.n3-tango-t13-mon3-24.why.2: (c) 調子 is a noun meaning “condition” or “form,” as in 「体の調子」. It cannot form the verb 「音量を調子する」.
default.q.n3-tango-t13-mon3-24.why.3: (d) 調節 means “adjust, regulate.” It combines with 「音量を調節する」 to mean adjusting the volume to an appropriate level, so it is completely correct.
default.q.n3-tango-t13-mon3-25.explanation:
- Sentence translation: I am so worried about my mother, who is in the hospital, that I cannot sleep.
- Related vocabulary and kanji:
  + 入院中: in the hospital, currently hospitalized.
  + 気になる: feel worried about, be concerned about, keep thinking about (a very common set expression).
  + 眠れない: be unable to sleep (the negative potential form of 眠る).
- Common expressions with 気:
  + 気になる: feel worried or concerned spontaneously (母のことが気になる: I am worried about my mother).
  + 気にする: deliberately worry about or pay attention to something (あまり気にしないで: Don’t worry too much).
  + 気をつける: be careful, pay attention.
- Example:
  + 明日の面接の結果が気になって、昨夜はよく眠れなかった。(I was worried about the result of tomorrow’s interview, so I could not sleep well last night.)
default.q.n3-tango-t13-mon3-25.why.0: (a) 気: It combines to form the idiomatic expression 「気になる」, meaning “to worry,” “to be concerned,” or “to weigh on one's mind.” This fits the context of being so worried about one's hospitalized mother that one cannot sleep.
default.q.n3-tango-t13-mon3-25.why.1: (b) 頭: There is no expression 「頭になる」 meaning “to worry”; there are only expressions such as 「頭に来る」 (get angry) and 「頭を使う」 (think/use one’s brain).
default.q.n3-tango-t13-mon3-25.why.2: (c) 心: There is no expression 「心になる」used in this context to express worry.
default.q.n3-tango-t13-mon3-25.why.3: (d) 身: Usually appears in expressions such as 「相手の身になる」 (put oneself in another person’s position) or 「親身になる」 (be considerate and attentive); it does not mean worrying or being concerned.
default.q.n3-tango-t13-mon4-26.verdict: The correct answer is 1. 簡単だ (simple, easy).
default.q.n3-tango-t13-mon4-26.explanation:
- Translation of the sentence: “This work is easy/light.”
- Related meanings:
  + 楽: comfortable, easy, relaxing
  + 簡単: simple, easy
  + 得意: one's forte, something one is good at
  + 楽しい: enjoyable, fun
  + 険しい: steep, harsh, severe
- Distinguishing 「楽（な）」and「楽しい」: Although both are written with 楽, 「楽しい」expresses a feeling of enjoyment or excitement, whereas 「楽（な）」expresses comfort, ease, or a lack of physical or mental effort. Therefore, 「仕事が楽だ」means that the work is easy and not demanding (簡単だ).
- Example: 「この作業はボタンを押すだけだからとても楽だ（簡単だ）。」(This task is very easy because all you have to do is press a button.)
default.q.n3-tango-t13-mon4-26.why.0: (a) 「簡単だ」 (“simple, easy to do”) means uncomplicated and requiring little effort, making it the best replacement for 「楽だ」 (“easy, comfortable, or not burdensome”) when describing the nature of the work.
default.q.n3-tango-t13-mon4-26.why.1: (b) 「得意だ」 means “be good at” or “be one's strength,” describing a person's ability or strength in something. It is not used to describe the easygoing nature of a job.
default.q.n3-tango-t13-mon4-26.why.2: (c) 「楽しい」(fun, enjoyable) describes a feeling of pleasure or excitement, whereas 「楽だ」here emphasizes ease and requiring little effort; it does not necessarily imply enjoyment.
default.q.n3-tango-t13-mon4-26.why.3: (d) 「険しい」 means “rugged, steep, severe” and describes difficult mountainous terrain or a stern expression; it is unrelated to the meaning “leisurely.”
default.q.n3-tango-t13-mon4-27.verdict: The correct answer is 2. 素敵な (wonderful, charming, elegant).
default.q.n3-tango-t13-mon4-27.explanation:
- Sentence translation: “Mr. Tanaka’s wife is an elegant woman.”
- Kanji-based vocabulary:
  + 上品: elegant, refined, classy (the antonym is 下品: vulgar, crude)
  + 平気: calm, composed, unbothered
  + 素敵: wonderful, charming, lovely
  + 正直: honest, straightforward
- Analysis: 「上品な人」 praises someone with an elegant air, polite manners, and refined clothing. Among the four choices, 「素敵な人」 (“a wonderful, charming person”) is the most natural and closest in its complimentary nuance, describing a person’s qualities and bearing.
- Example: 「彼女の上品な（素敵な）立ち振る舞いに見とれてしまった。」(I was captivated by her elegant, wonderful manner.)
default.q.n3-tango-t13-mon4-27.why.0: (a) 「平気な」(calm, unconcerned, unaffected) describes an attitude of not worrying or being bothered by difficulties or incidents. It does not mean elegant or refined.
default.q.n3-tango-t13-mon4-27.why.1: (b) 「素敵な」 (“wonderful, charming, attractive”) is a positive adjective describing a person’s elegant manner and favorable impression, making it the best replacement for 「上品な」 (“refined, elegant”).
default.q.n3-tango-t13-mon4-27.why.2: (c) 「得意な」 means being good at something or confident in one’s strength; it does not praise someone’s refined manner or dignified character.
default.q.n3-tango-t13-mon4-27.why.3: (d) 「正直な」(honest, truthful) describes a sincere and straightforward personality, which differs from the refined appearance or graceful manner described by 「上品な」.
default.q.n3-tango-t13-mon4-28.verdict: The correct answer is 4. やりかた (way of doing something, method).
default.q.n3-tango-t13-mon4-28.explanation:
- Sentence translation: "I tried many different methods (ways of doing things)."
- Sino-Japanese vocabulary:
  + 方法: method, way = やり方 (way of doing something)
  + 種類: type, kind
  + 都合: convenience, circumstances/time constraints
  + 具合: condition, state (of one's health, a machine, etc.)
  + 試す: to try, to test
- 「方法」 is a Sino-Japanese noun meaning a method or way of carrying out something, and is completely synonymous with the native Japanese noun 「やり方（やりかた）」 (way of doing something).
- Example: 「日本語を上達させるいい方法（やり方）を探している。」 (I am looking for a good way to improve my Japanese.)
default.q.n3-tango-t13-mon4-28.why.0: (a) 「しゅるい」 (種類): Means “type” or “category” and is used to classify objects or things; it does not mean a method or way of doing something.
default.q.n3-tango-t13-mon4-28.why.1: (b) 「つごう」 (都合) refers to convenience or one's schedule and circumstances, especially in terms of time; it cannot replace a method.
default.q.n3-tango-t13-mon4-28.why.2: (c) 「ぐあい」 (具合: condition, state) refers to a person's health or the operating condition of machinery. It does not mean method or manner.
default.q.n3-tango-t13-mon4-28.why.3: (d) 「やりかた」 (やり方, the way of doing something) directly corresponds in meaning to 「方法」 (method). It describes how to carry out an activity, so it is a perfect substitute in this sentence.
default.q.n3-tango-t13-mon4-29.verdict: The correct answer is 3. むすんで (connect, join).
default.q.n3-tango-t13-mon4-29.explanation:
- Sentence translation: "The tunnel is connecting Hokkaido and Honshu."
- Kanji-based vocabulary:
  + 繋ぐ: to connect, tie, or link (ている-form: つないでいる)
  + 結ぶ: to tie, connect, or link (て-form: むすんで)
  + 並ぶ: to line up, stand side by side
  + 運ぶ: to transport, carry
  + 浮かぶ: to float, rise to the surface
- Both verbs 「つなぐ」 and 「結ぶ」 commonly appear in the pattern 「AとBをつなぐ / 結ぶ」 to describe a bridge, route, or tunnel connecting two places or regions. (In this sentence, the reference is to the Seikan Tunnel connecting Honshu and Hokkaido.)
- Example: 「この橋は島と本土を結んでいる（つないでいる）。」 (This bridge connects the island with the mainland.)
default.q.n3-tango-t13-mon4-29.why.0: (a) 「ならんで」 (並ぶ — line up, stand side by side) describes objects standing next to one another in a row; it does not mean connecting two locations.
default.q.n3-tango-t13-mon4-29.why.1: (b) 「はこんで」 (運ぶ) means carrying or transporting a person or object from one place to another; it does not mean connecting routes.
default.q.n3-tango-t13-mon4-29.why.2: (c) 「むすんで」 (結ぶ—link, connect) is synonymous with 「つなぐ」 when describing a bridge, tunnel, or road connecting two locations (AとBを結ぶ/つなぐ).
default.q.n3-tango-t13-mon4-29.why.3: (d) 「うかんで」 (浮かぶ—float, come to mind) refers to something floating on water or a thought occurring to someone; it is unrelated to connecting things.
default.q.n3-tango-t13-mon4-30.verdict: The correct answer is 1. 本当は (actually, in truth).
default.q.n3-tango-t13-mon4-30.explanation:
- Sentence translation: “Actually, I was planning to go home tomorrow too.”
- Kanji-based vocabulary:
  + 実は (actually, the truth is)
  + 本当は (actually, in fact)
  + 勿論 (of course, naturally)
  + 非常に (extremely, very)
  + 偶に (occasionally, sometimes)
- Both 「実は（じつは）」 and 「本当は（ほんとうは）」 are adverbs used at the beginning of a sentence when the speaker wants to reveal or confess a fact, actual circumstance, or plan that they had not previously told the listener.
- Example: 「実は（本当は）、その話を知っていました。」 (Actually, I already knew about that.)
default.q.n3-tango-t13-mon4-30.why.0: (a) 「本当は」 (actually, in fact) is synonymous with 「じつは」 (実は) and is used at the beginning of a statement when revealing a truth or one's actual plan to the other person.
default.q.n3-tango-t13-mon4-30.why.1: (b) 「もちろん」 (“of course,” “naturally”) is used to affirm that something is obvious and beyond dispute; it is not used to introduce a personal statement of fact.
default.q.n3-tango-t13-mon4-30.why.2: (c) 「非常に」 (“very, extremely”) is an adverb indicating a high degree of a state or action; it does not mean “in reality” or “the fact is.”
default.q.n3-tango-t13-mon4-30.why.3: (d) 「たまに」 means “occasionally” or “sometimes.” It is an adverb indicating low frequency and has nothing to do with revealing information.
default.q.n3-tango-t13-mon5-31.verdict: The correct answer is 2: あしたは京都へ参ります。
default.q.n3-tango-t13-mon5-31.explanation:
• **参る (まいる)** is the humble form (humble language, kenjōgo I) of **行く (to go)** and **来る (to come)**. It is used for actions performed by the speaker or someone on the speaker's side (family members or colleagues from the same company) to humble oneself and show respect to the other person.
• Sentence 2 translates as: *"I will go to Kyoto tomorrow."* (Using the humble form `参る` instead of `行きます` for the speaker's action is completely correct.)
• **Related vocabulary and kanji meanings**:
  - 参る (まいる): to go, to come (humble form); it can also mean to be defeated, surrender, or feel exhausted (参った).
  - いらっしゃる: the respectful form of 行く/来る/居る.
• **Additional example**:
  - ただいま、担当の者がそちらへ**参ります**。 (The person in charge will come over to you right away.)
default.q.n3-tango-t13-mon5-31.why.0: (a) Incorrect because expressing “stay at home all day” requires a verb indicating a state of being or remaining somewhere, such as 居る (the humble form is おる), not 参る, which means to go or come.
default.q.n3-tango-t13-mon5-31.why.1: (b) Correct because 参る is the humble form of 行く/来る, used when the speaker humbles their own act of going to Kyoto to express politeness.
default.q.n3-tango-t13-mon5-31.why.2: (c) Correct. 彼のお父さん (his father, another person) is someone who should be respected, so the humble verb 参る must not be used; a respectful expression such as いらっしゃいました or おいでになりました is required.
default.q.n3-tango-t13-mon5-31.why.3: (d) Incorrect because asking the listener “Where are you going now?” requires an honorific expression such as いらっしゃいますか or 行かれますか. The humble form 参る is not used for the other person.
default.q.n3-tango-t13-mon5-32.verdict: The correct answer is 1: 会社を休んでみんなに迷惑をかけた。
default.q.n3-tango-t13-mon5-32.explanation:
• **迷惑 (めいわく)** means trouble, inconvenience, or annoyance caused to another person.
• It commonly appears in fixed expressions and patterns:
  - **〜に迷惑をかける**: cause trouble or inconvenience for someone.
  - **〜の迷惑になる**: become a nuisance to someone.
  - **ご迷惑をおかけします**: I apologize for causing you trouble (honorific expression).
• Sentence 1 translation: *“I took time off work and caused trouble for everyone.”*
• **Related vocabulary**:
  - 迷惑 (めいわく): trouble, inconvenience.
  - 迷う (まよう): lose one’s way, be unsure, hesitate.
• **Additional example**:
  - 夜遅くに大きな音を立てると、近所の人に**迷惑**がかかります。 (Making loud noises late at night will disturb the neighbors.)
default.q.n3-tango-t13-mon5-32.why.0: (a) Correct because 迷惑をかける (to cause trouble, inconvenience others) is the standard idiomatic expression for taking time off work and affecting everyone at the company.
default.q.n3-tango-t13-mon5-32.why.1: (b) Incorrect because expressing uncertainty or indecision when choosing requires the verb 迷う (迷っている) or 悩む, not 迷惑.
default.q.n3-tango-t13-mon5-32.why.2: (c) Incorrect. To express “not having a dictionary would not cause difficulty or inconvenience,” use 困らない or 不便ではない, not 迷惑しない.
default.q.n3-tango-t13-mon5-32.why.3: (d) Incorrect because expressing “no matter how much I look it up, it is useless / I cannot understand it” requires 無駄だ or 分からない, not 迷惑だ.
default.q.n3-tango-t13-mon5-33.verdict: The correct answer is 4: 道端で財布を拾ったので、交番に届けた。
default.q.n3-tango-t13-mon5-33.explanation:
• **拾う (ひろう)** means literally “to pick up,” as in picking up an object that has fallen on the ground. It also has extended meanings such as picking up or hailing a taxi (タクシーを拾う) and narrowly escaping or salvaging something (命を拾う).
• Sentence 4: *“Because I picked up a wallet by the roadside, I took it to the police box and handed it in.”*
• **Related vocabulary and kanji**:
  - 拾う (ひろう): to pick up, gather.
  - 道端 (みちばた): roadside, edge of the street.
  - 交番 (こうばん): police box.
  - 届ける (とどける): to deliver, hand in, report.
• **Additional example**:
  - 道でクレジットカードを**拾った**ので、警察に届けました。 (I picked up a credit card on the street, so I handed it in to the police.)
default.q.n3-tango-t13-mon5-33.why.0: (a) Incorrect because seeing recruitment information in a newspaper is expressed with 見つけた (found/saw) or 目に入った, not 拾った.
default.q.n3-tango-t13-mon5-33.why.1: (b) Incorrect because when someone ultimately buys or obtains a new car, 買った (bought) or 手に入れた (obtained) is used, not 拾った.
default.q.n3-tango-t13-mon5-33.why.2: (c) Incorrect because when listening and taking notes at the same time, the expression メモを取る (メモを取りながら) is used; Japanese does not use メモを拾う.
default.q.n3-tango-t13-mon5-33.why.3: (d) Correct. 拾う means to pick up something that has fallen on the ground; here, “picking up a wallet found by the roadside” (道端で財布を拾う) is the most accurate context.
default.q.n3-tango-t13-mon5-34.verdict: The correct answer is 1: 大変お世話になりました。
default.q.n3-tango-t13-mon5-34.explanation:
• **世話 (せわ - THẾ THOẠI)** means care, help, concern, or looking after someone or something.
• Important fixed expressions:
  - **お世話になる / 大変お世話になりました**: to receive someone's help / Thank you very much for all your help (a common greeting or expression of gratitude).
  - **〜の世話をする**: to take care of or look after someone or something (such as an elderly person, child, or pet). Note: use `世話をする` or `面倒を見る` for "take care of"; do not incorrectly combine them as `世話を見る`.
  - **世話が焼ける**: to require a lot of care and attention (because the person is clumsy or incapable).
• Sentence 1 translates as: *"Thank you very much for all your help during this time."*
• Additional example:
  - 母は毎朝早く起きて、入院している祖父の**世話**をしています。 (My mother gets up early every morning to take care of my grandfather, who is in the hospital.)

- さっさと: quickly, promptly, without dawdling (often used to urge someone or indicate decisive action).
- 早く (はやく): quickly, soon (expressing urgency or the need to do something immediately).
- 片付ける (かたづける): tidy up, put in order (片付けなさい is a mild imperative: clean it up).
- 凄い (すごく): very, extremely (indicating a high degree).
- 短い (みじかい → みじかく): short (in length, size, or duration).
- 細かい (こまかい → こまかく): detailed, meticulous, small.

Example:
- さっさとご飯を食べてしまいなさい。 (Hurry up and finish your meal.)
= 早くご飯を食べてしまいなさい。
default.q.n3-tango-t14-mon4-30.why.0: (a) 「すごく」 means very or extremely, indicating degree; it does not mean quickly or urgently.
default.q.n3-tango-t14-mon4-30.why.1: (b) 「みじかく」 means “short” in length or duration; it is not used to urge someone to work faster.
default.q.n3-tango-t14-mon4-30.why.2: (c) 「はやく」 means “quickly,” “promptly,” or “hurry”; it accurately substitutes for the adverb 「さっさと」 in a reminder or prompt to do something immediately.
default.q.n3-tango-t14-mon4-30.why.3: (d) 「こまかく」means in detail, meticulously, or thoroughly; it does not mean acting urgently in terms of time or speed.
default.q.n3-tango-t14-mon5-31.verdict: The correct answer is choice 2: 忘年会でお酒を飲んで騒いだ。
default.q.n3-tango-t14-mon5-31.explanation:
- **騒ぐ**: to make noise, cause a commotion, make a racket, or fool around noisily (or to cause public alarm or agitation in a social context).
- **Related kanji-based terms**:
  + 騒: 騒音 (noise), 物騒 (dangerous, unsettling).
  + 忘年会: year-end party.
- **Detailed explanation**: 「騒ぐ」 is an intransitive verb describing people shouting, making noise, or having a lively time together (especially at drinking parties or celebrations), or causing a disturbance in a public place.
- **Additional example**:
  + 教室で大声で騒いではいけません。(You must not make a lot of noise in the classroom.)
default.q.n3-tango-t14-mon5-31.why.0: (a) Incorrect because leaves moving in the wind are described with 「揺れる」 (to sway or tremble) or 「ざわめく」 (to rustle), not 「騒ぐ」.
default.q.n3-tango-t14-mon5-31.why.1: (b) Correct because 「お酒を飲んで騒ぐ」 is a natural collocation meaning to drink alcohol and then chat, joke, and make merry noisily at a year-end party.
default.q.n3-tango-t14-mon5-31.why.2: (c) Incorrect because a twinkling star is described with 「光っている」 or 「輝いている」; 「騒ぐ」 cannot be used for starlight.
default.q.n3-tango-t14-mon5-31.why.3: (d) Incorrect in grammar and word choice. 「騒ぐ」 is an intransitive verb and does not take 「～を」. To tell someone not to bother or disturb one’s father, use 「邪魔しないでください」.
default.q.n3-tango-t14-mon5-32.verdict: The correct answer is choice 2: 彼女は活力に溢れている。
default.q.n3-tango-t14-mon5-32.explanation:
- **活力**: vitality, energy, vigor.
- **Related kanji**:
  + 活: 活動 (activity), 活躍 (to play an active role, to perform brilliantly).
  + 力: 体力 (physical strength), 気力 (mental energy, motivation).
- **Common collocations**:
  + 活力に溢れている / 活力に満ちている: to be brimming with vitality, to be full of energy.
  + 活力が湧く: for one's energy to well up.
  + 活力を取り戻す: to regain one's vitality.
- **Additional example**:
  + 朝の運動は一日の活力を生み出してくれる。(Morning exercise gives you energy for the entire day.)
default.q.n3-tango-t14-mon5-32.why.0: (a) Seismic activity should be expressed with 「活動」 (地震活動: seismic activity), not 「活力」.
default.q.n3-tango-t14-mon5-32.why.1: (b) Correct, because 「活力に溢れている」 (be full of vitality) is a standard and very common expression for describing someone energetic and enthusiastic.
default.q.n3-tango-t14-mon5-32.why.2: (c) Incorrect. To say that someone performed outstandingly or shone in the final, use 「大活躍した」, not 「大活力する」, which is not a word.
default.q.n3-tango-t14-mon5-32.why.3: (d) Incorrect because describing the mother's cheerful, healthy lifestyle requires an adverb or adjective such as 「元気に暮らしている」 (living healthily) or 「穏やかに」 (peacefully), not 「活力に」.
default.q.n3-tango-t14-mon5-33.verdict: The correct answer is choice 1: 寝る前に時計のタイマーをセットした。
default.q.n3-tango-t14-mon5-33.explanation:
• **セット (set)**:
  1. To set or configure settings, timers, alarms, etc.: 「タイマー／アラーム／時間をセットする」.
  2. To style one’s hair: 「髪をセットする」.
  3. A set or combo containing several items: 「セットメニュー」(set meal), 「コーヒーとケーキのセット」.
- **Detailed analysis**: In sentence 1, 「タイマーをセットする」is a loanword expression meaning “set the timer,” and is perfectly standard in everyday Japanese.
- **Additional example**:
  + 毎晩寝る前に目覚まし時計を6時にセットする。(Every night before going to bed, I set my alarm clock for 6:00.)
default.q.n3-tango-t14-mon5-33.why.0: (a) Correct because 「タイマーをセットする」 (to set a timer) is the standard and most commonly used expression with 「セット」.
default.q.n3-tango-t14-mon5-33.why.1: (b) Incorrect because when clothes and shoes are laid out at the entrance in advance, verbs such as 「用意した」(prepared) or 「並べた」(arranged) should be used, not 「セットした」.
default.q.n3-tango-t14-mon5-33.why.2: (c) is incorrect because a motorcycle that is repaired or newly purchased would use 「修理した」, 「買った」, or 「整備した」. 「セットした」 does not mean assembling or maintaining a motorcycle.
default.q.n3-tango-t14-mon5-33.why.3: (d) Incorrect because composing music for a song requires 「作曲した」, not 「セットした」.
default.q.n3-tango-t14-mon5-34.verdict: The correct answer is choice 2: 送料をふくめて2500円になる。
default.q.n3-tango-t14-mon5-34.explanation:
- **含める (HÀM)**: include, count as part of the total (transitive verb).
- **Related kanji readings and compounds**:
  + 含 (HÀM): 含有 (contain), 含まれる (intransitive verb: be included).
  + 送料 (TỐNG LIỆU): shipping fee, postage.
- **Common structure**:
  + ～を含めて: including... (example: 消費税を含めて - including consumption tax).
- **Additional example**:
  + 私を含めて、家族は全員で5人です。(Including me, there are five people in my family.)
default.q.n3-tango-t14-mon5-34.why.0: (a) Incorrect because to add or season soup with salt to make the flavor stronger, use 「入れて」 (put in) or 「加えて」 (add), not 「含めて」.
default.q.n3-tango-t14-mon5-34.why.1: (b) Correct because 「送料を含めて」 means “including the shipping fee.” This is an extremely common pattern when calculating the total cost.
default.q.n3-tango-t14-mon5-34.why.2: (c) Incorrect because the standard expression for everyone joining forces is 「力を合わせて」, not 「力を含める」.
default.q.n3-tango-t14-mon5-34.why.3: (d) Incorrect because choosing a tie to match the color of a suit requires 「スーツの色に合わせて」 (according to/in harmony with), not 「含めて」.
default.q.n3-tango-t14-mon5-35.verdict: The correct answer is choice 4: いちいち説明する必要はない。
default.q.n3-tango-t14-mon5-35.explanation:
- **いちいち**: every little detail, every single thing, one by one (often implying criticism, annoyance, or unnecessary fuss when someone interferes with or explains trivial matters too thoroughly).
- **Related kanji compounds**:
  + 逐: 逐次 (successively), 逐条 (item by item).
  + 説明: explanation.
- **Common expressions**:
  + いちいち文句を言う: to complain about every little thing, to nitpick.
  + いちいち気にする: to worry about every little thing.
  + いちいち説明する: to explain every single detail.
- **Additional example**:
  + 小さな失敗についていちいち口を出さないでほしい。(I wish you would stop commenting on and criticizing every little mistake.)
default.q.n3-tango-t14-mon5-35.why.0: (a) Incorrect because the bus’s prolonged delay makes people irritated and impatient, so an onomatopoeic word expressing a mental state such as 「いらいらした」must be used, not 「いちいちした」.
default.q.n3-tango-t14-mon5-35.why.1: (b) Incorrect because the adverb 「いよいよ」means “finally” or “at last” and is used to express that starting work tomorrow is imminent; 「いちいち」does not have this meaning.
default.q.n3-tango-t14-mon5-35.why.2: (c) Incorrect. 「いちいち」 is an adverb, not a だ-ending adjective; to praise someone’s running form, use 「かっこいい」 (“good-looking, impressive”) or 「素晴らしい」 (“excellent”).
default.q.n3-tango-t14-mon5-35.why.3: (d) Correct because「いちいち説明する」(explain every single detail, including trivial matters) is a standard and natural usage in Japanese.
default.q.n3-tango-t15-mon1-1.verdict: The correct answer is 3. しゅうきょう.

default.q.n3-tango-t15-mon1-2.why.1: (b) Incorrect. けしき is the reading of 景色 (scenery).
default.q.n3-tango-t15-mon1-2.why.2: (c) Correct. 田舎 has the special reading (jukujikun) いなか and means the countryside or a rural area.

default.q.n3-tango-t15-mon1-3.explanation:

- Vocabulary and kanji-based meanings:

  + Antonym: 下着 (したぎ): underwear.

default.q.n3-tango-t15-mon1-3.why.0: (a) Incorrect because 上 undergoes a sound change in this word and is read うわ, as in 上着 (うわぎ) and 上書き (うわがき), not うえ.
default.q.n3-tango-t15-mon1-3.why.1: (b) Incorrect because 着 is read as ちゃく/じゃく in on-reading, but in 上着, 着 is read as ぎ through a sound change in kun-reading.
default.q.n3-tango-t15-mon1-3.why.2: (c) Incorrect because it improperly combines a kun-reading (うえ) with an on-reading (ちゃく).
default.q.n3-tango-t15-mon1-3.why.3: (d) Correct. 上着 is read うわぎ: 上 is read うわ, and 着 is read ぎ, a sound change from き in きる/着る.
default.q.n3-tango-t15-mon1-4.verdict: The correct answer is 2. ゆずった.

default.q.n3-tango-t15-mon1-6.verdict: The correct answer is 4. べんとう.
default.q.n3-tango-t15-mon1-6.explanation:
- Meaning: My mother makes me a boxed lunch every day.
- Vocabulary and kanji:

  + 弁: on-reading べん, as in 弁護士 - べんごし: lawyer.

default.q.n3-tango-t15-mon1-6.why.3: (d) Correct. 弁当 is read with on-readings as べんとう (弁 [べん] and 当 [とう], with a long vowel).
default.q.n3-tango-t15-mon1-7.verdict: The correct answer is 1. たつ.

- Vocabulary & Sino-Japanese readings:

  + 夢中 (MỘNG TRUNG) - むちゅう: absorbed, engrossed (夢中になる: become absorbed).

default.q.n3-tango-t15-mon1-7.why.0: (a) Correct. 経つ is read with the kun-reading たつ and is used to describe time passing.

default.q.n3-tango-t15-mon1-7.why.3: (d) Incorrect. かつ is 勝つ (to win).

default.q.n3-tango-t15-mon1-8.explanation:

- Vocabulary and kanji analysis:
  + 発表 (はっぴょう): to present, announce, publish; presentation (発表する).
  + 論文 (ろんぶん): thesis, academic paper.

default.q.n3-tango-t15-mon1-8.why.0: (a) Incorrect because it lacks the geminate consonant and does not undergo the /p/ handakuten change (it should be はっぴょう, not はつひょう).
default.q.n3-tango-t15-mon1-8.why.1: (b) Correct. 発表 (presentation) is read はっぴょう in on-reading: 発 [はつ] and 表 [ひょう] combine, causing a geminate sound and the change to ぴょう.

default.q.n3-tango-t15-mon2-9.verdict: The correct answer is 1. 車掌 (しゃしょう - conductor, train conductor).
default.q.n3-tango-t15-mon2-9.explanation:
- **Sentence translation**: "The conductor said to me, 'May I check your ticket?'"
- **Kanji analysis**:
  - **車掌** (しゃしょう): conductor, ticket inspector on a train or bus. **車** means vehicles, while **掌** means palm, to hold, or to manage; for example, 掌握（しょうあく） means to grasp or control.
  - **社長** (しゃちょう): company president. Be careful to distinguish the readings *しょう* and *ちょう.
- **Related vocabulary**:
  - 切符 (きっぷ): ticket for a vehicle or train.
  - 拝見する (はいけんする): to look at, to see; the humble form of 見る.

default.q.n3-tango-t15-mon2-9.why.0: (a) 車掌 is the correct word, referring to a conductor or ticket inspector on a train or bus.
default.q.n3-tango-t15-mon2-9.why.1: (b) 車長 is formed from 車 and 長 and is read as しゃちょう; it does not mean a ticket inspector.
default.q.n3-tango-t15-mon2-9.why.2: (c) 社掌 is incorrect because the kanji 社 is wrong; this word does not exist in Japanese.
default.q.n3-tango-t15-mon2-9.why.3: (d) 社長 is read しゃちょう and means company president; both the kanji and the meaning are incorrect.
default.q.n3-tango-t15-mon2-10.verdict: The correct answer is 3. 往復 (round trip, going and returning).
default.q.n3-tango-t15-mon2-10.explanation:
- **Sentence meaning**: "For work, I travel between Guangzhou and Tokyo once a month, making a round trip."
- **Kanji analysis**:
  - **往復** (おうふく): round trip, going and returning. **往** means going toward, as in 往来, while **復** means returning or repeating, as in 復習 and 回復. Both kanji contain the 彳 radical, associated with walking.
- **Easily confused kanji**:
  - **復** (彳 radical: returning) in 往復 and 回復.
  - **複** (衤 radical: double or multiple) in 複雑 and 複合.
- **Opposite vocabulary**: 片道 (かたみち: one way) >< 往復 (おうふく: two way, round trip).
- **Example**: 往復切符を買うと、片道ずつ買うより少し安くなります。(Buying a round-trip ticket is slightly cheaper than buying the two one-way tickets separately.)
default.q.n3-tango-t15-mon2-10.why.0: (a) 往複 is incorrect because 複 uses the 衤 radical, as in 複雑. The correct character is 復, which contains the 彳 radical.
default.q.n3-tango-t15-mon2-10.why.1: (b) 応複 has both kanji wrong: 応 and 複.
default.q.n3-tango-t15-mon2-10.why.2: (c) 往復 is the correct spelling. Both 往 and 復 contain the 彳 radical, and the word refers to going and coming back.
default.q.n3-tango-t15-mon2-10.why.3: (d) 応復 has the kanji 応 wrong (as in 応援 — cheering, and 応用 — application).
default.q.n3-tango-t15-mon2-11.verdict: The correct answer is 1. 無料 (free of charge).
default.q.n3-tango-t15-mon2-11.explanation:
- **Translation of the sentence:** Citizens aged 70 and over can use the bus free of charge.
- **Kanji analysis:**
  - **無料** (むりょう): free of charge, costing nothing. Here, **無** means “without” or “none” (as in 無理: unreasonable, excessive; 無視: to ignore), while **料** means “fee,” “cost,” or “charge” (as in 料金: fee; 料理: cooking, dish).
  - **無量** (むりょう): immeasurable, infinite; commonly seen in the idiom 感慨無量 (かんがいむりょう: being overwhelmed with emotion).
- **Synonyms and antonyms:**
  - Synonyms: ただ (free of charge), フリー (free).
  - Antonym: 有料 (ゆうりょう: fee-charging, not free).

default.q.n3-tango-t16-mon3-15.explanation:
Sentence meaning: “This question is inexplicably difficult. I’ll go ask the teacher and see what they say.”

Analysis:
The adverb 「どうも」when used with an adjective or adverb often expresses a vague feeling whose specific cause is unclear (“somehow / for some reason / it seems”). In this sentence, the speaker finds the exercise strangely difficult and decides to ask the teacher.

Kanji vocabulary:
- 問題: question, exercise, problem
- 難: difficult
- 先生: teacher

default.q.n3-tango-t16-mon3-15.why.1: (b) 「どうにか」 means “somehow” or “manage to,” and commonly appears in expressions such as どうにかなる (things will somehow work out) or どうにか間に合う (somehow make it on time). It does not modify an adjective expressing degree as it does here.
default.q.n3-tango-t16-mon3-15.why.2: (c) 「どうして」 means “why,” and is used in questions or exclamations expressing doubt. It does not precede an adjective as an adverbial modifier in this declarative sentence.
default.q.n3-tango-t16-mon3-15.why.3: (d) 「どうやら」 means “it seems” or “apparently” and is usually accompanied by an inferential ending such as 〜ようだ or 〜らしい (e.g., どうやら雨が降るらしい). It does not directly precede an adjective in this declarative sentence.

もっと**具体的な**例を挙げて説明してください。(Please give a more specific example to explain it.)
default.q.n3-tango-t16-mon3-23.why.0: (a) 「批判的」（ひはんてき） means "critical" or "disapproving," with a negative or strongly argumentative nuance. It is not the most common collocation for making constructive suggestions in everyday situations.
default.q.n3-tango-t16-mon3-23.why.1: (b) 「積極的」 means “positive, proactive” and usually modifies an attitude or action, such as 積極的な態度 or 積極的に参加する. It is less natural when directly combined as 「積極的な意見」.
default.q.n3-tango-t16-mon3-23.why.2: (c) 「具体的」（ぐたいてき） means “specific, concrete,” and 「具体的な意見」 (a specific opinion with clear data and solutions) is the most natural and accurate usage.
default.q.n3-tango-t16-mon3-23.why.3: (d) 「抽象的」（ちゅうしょうてき） means “abstract” or “vague,” and is often used to criticize a general, impractical opinion. It is not a quality that is highly valued when expressing an opinion.
default.q.n3-tango-t16-mon3-24.explanation:
Translation: “The setting of this novel is modern-day Tokyo.”

Analysis:
The noun 「舞台」（ぶたい） literally means a performance stage, but its very common figurative meaning is the setting—the place and time in which the story of a literary or artistic work takes place, such as a novel, film, or play. The pattern 「〜の舞台は...だ」 (“the setting of … is …”) is a standard fixed expression.

Kanji:
- 小説: novel
- 舞台: stage, setting
- 現代: modern times, the present day
- 東京: Tokyo

Example:
この映画は19世紀のパリを**舞台**にしている。(This film is set in nineteenth-century Paris.)
default.q.n3-tango-t16-mon3-24.why.0: (a) 「場面」（ばめん） means "a scene, situation, or specific setting" (such as 映画の感動的な場面 - a moving scene in a movie). It does not refer to the entire space and time serving as the main setting of a work.
default.q.n3-tango-t16-mon3-24.why.1: (b) 「舞台」（ぶたい） means not only “stage” but also the “setting” of a literary or artistic work (such as 小説の舞台, “the setting of a novel”), so it is completely accurate.
default.q.n3-tango-t16-mon3-24.why.2: (c) 「場所」（ばしょ）means “place/location” and is used for an actual everyday geographical location, such as 待ち合わせの場所. It is not a term for an artistic setting.
default.q.n3-tango-t16-mon3-24.why.3: (d) 「風景」(ふうけい) means “scenery” or “landscape,” and is used to describe the beauty of natural surroundings or streets. It is not used for the overall setting of a novel.
default.q.n3-tango-t16-mon3-25.explanation:
Meaning: "Because it started raining, I brought the laundry indoors (into the room)."

Analysis:
「室内」（しつない） refers to the inside of a room or house (opposite of outdoors or outside a balcony: 室外 / 屋外). In everyday Japanese life, bringing laundry indoors to dry when it rains is expressed as 「室内に入れる」 or 「室内干し」（しつないぼし）.

Kanji-based vocabulary:
- 雨 (VŨ): rain
- 降る (GIÁNG/HÀNG): fall, come down (rain)
- 洗濯物 (TẨY TRẠC VẬT): laundry
- 室内 (THẤT NỘI): indoors, inside a room

Example:
雨の日は洗濯物を**室内**に干すことが多い。(On rainy days, I often hang the laundry indoors.)
default.q.n3-tango-t16-mon3-25.why.0: (a) 「屋内」（おくない） means “indoors” and contrasts with 屋外 (“outdoors”). It is commonly used for public facilities, large-scale structures, or indoor sports facilities (such as 屋内プール), and is less common in household situations such as collecting laundry.
default.q.n3-tango-t16-mon3-25.why.1: (b) 「室内」（しつない） means "indoors" or "inside a room," describing the space inside a house, in contrast to a balcony or the outdoors. It is the precise vocabulary for bringing laundry indoors when it rains.
default.q.n3-tango-t16-mon3-25.why.2: (c) 「玄関」（げんかん）means the entrance or entryway of a house, where shoes are removed. It is not the appropriate place to bring in and hang or store laundry.
default.q.n3-tango-t16-mon3-25.why.3: (d) 「部屋」（へや） means “room” and is commonly used in everyday conversation, but in the test’s contrast between indoor and outdoor spaces, 「室内」 is more precise and specialized.
default.q.n3-tango-t16-mon4-26.verdict: The correct answer is 1. 気をつけて.
default.q.n3-tango-t16-mon4-26.explanation:
- Sentence meaning: “He always acts cautiously.”
- Vocabulary: 慎重 (しんちょう: cautious, careful, and thoughtful before taking action), 行動 (こうどう: action).
- 「慎重に」 is synonymous with 「気をつけて」(carefully, with caution).

default.q.n3-tango-t16-mon4-26.why.0: (a) 「気をつけて」 means “be careful, pay attention” and is the most appropriate synonym and substitute for 「慎重に」 (“carefully, cautiously”) in this context.
default.q.n3-tango-t16-mon4-26.why.1: (b) 「あわてて」 means “hurriedly, flusteredly, in a panic,” showing a lack of composure and contrasting with a careful action.
default.q.n3-tango-t16-mon4-26.why.2: (c) 「いそいで」means “hurriedly” or “in haste,” emphasizing speed and time pressure; it does not express carefulness or caution.
default.q.n3-tango-t16-mon4-26.why.3: (d) 「のんびり」 means “relaxed, leisurely, carefree,” describing a comfortable, unhurried state; it does not mean careful or cautious.
default.q.n3-tango-t16-mon4-27.verdict: The correct answer is 2. つまらない.
default.q.n3-tango-t16-mon4-27.explanation:
- Sentence meaning: 「That is completely a pointless / ridiculous / worthless story.」
- Vocabulary:
  + くだらない: pointless, ridiculous, trivial, worthless.
  + つまらない: boring, dull, mediocre (it can replace くだらない when describing a worthless story or joke).
  + 全く (まったく): completely, utterly.
  + 話 (はなし): story.
- Expanded example: くだらない冗談はやめてください。(Please stop making such pointless jokes.) ＝ つまらない冗談はやめてください。
default.q.n3-tango-t16-mon4-27.why.0: (a) 「おもしろい」 means "interesting" or "fun," with a positive meaning opposite to 「くだらない」.
default.q.n3-tango-t16-mon4-27.why.1: (b) 「つまらない」 means “boring, dull, worthless.” It is a synonym that accurately replaces 「くだらない」 (“silly, pointless, of no value”).
default.q.n3-tango-t16-mon4-27.why.2: (c) 「たのしい」 means "fun, enjoyable, exciting" and does not express the negative meaning in the original sentence.
default.q.n3-tango-t16-mon4-27.why.3: (d) 「むずかしい」 means “difficult” or “complicated” and cannot express the idea that a story is pointless or nonsensical.
default.q.n3-tango-t16-mon4-28.verdict: The correct answer is 2. とても近い.
default.q.n3-tango-t16-mon4-28.explanation:
- Meaning of the sentence: "His house is extremely close to the station."
- Kanji and vocabulary:
  + 至近 (しきん): extremely close, at a very short distance (至 = reach, go as far as; 近 = near). It is commonly used in expressions such as 「至近の距離」「至近距離」(an extremely short distance).
  + 距離 (きょり): distance.
  + 駅 (えき): station.
- Extended example: 事故現場から至近の病院へ運ばれた。 (The victim was taken to a hospital very close to the accident scene.) ＝ 事故現場からとても近い病院へ運ばれた。
default.q.n3-tango-t16-mon4-28.why.0: (a) 「とても遠い」means "very far," which is the complete opposite of「至近」.
default.q.n3-tango-t16-mon4-28.why.1: (b) 「とても近い」 means “very close,” which precisely matches the meaning of 「至近の」 (extremely close).
default.q.n3-tango-t16-mon4-28.why.2: (c) 「とても広い」 means “very wide” or “very spacious,” referring to area or space, and is not used to describe the distance between two points.
default.q.n3-tango-t16-mon4-28.why.3: (d) 「とても狭い」 means “very narrow” or “cramped” and is not used to describe the length of a distance or route.
default.q.n3-tango-t16-mon4-29.verdict: The correct answer is 1. よてい.
default.q.n3-tango-t16-mon4-29.explanation:
- Sentence meaning: “Confirm tomorrow’s schedule / plans.”
- Kanji and vocabulary:
  + スケジュール: a loanword from English “schedule,” meaning a schedule or work/time plan.
  + 予定 (YOTEI): an intended plan, schedule, or arrangement made in advance.
  + 確認 (KAKUNIN): to check, confirm.
  + 明日 (ASHITA / ASU): tomorrow.

default.q.n3-tango-t16-mon4-29.why.0: (a) 「よてい」(予定) means "plan, schedule" and is the direct Japanese equivalent and a perfect replacement for the borrowed katakana word 「スケジュール」.
default.q.n3-tango-t16-mon4-29.why.1: (b) 「じかん」(時間) refers to a point in time or a period of time; it does not fully convey the meaning of a schedule or plan.
default.q.n3-tango-t16-mon4-29.why.2: (c) 「ばしょ」(場所) means "place" or "location" and is unrelated to a schedule.
default.q.n3-tango-t16-mon4-29.why.3: (d) 「きろく」(記録) means “record, documentation, achievement,” and does not express a plan intended for the future.
default.q.n3-tango-t16-mon4-30.verdict: The correct answer is 1. にわかに.
default.q.n3-tango-t16-mon4-30.explanation:
- Meaning of the sentence: “The sky suddenly became cloudy / turned gloomy.”
- Vocabulary and readings:
  + 急に (きゅうに): suddenly, all of a sudden, urgently.
  + にわかに (written 俄かに): suddenly, unexpectedly (often used for sudden changes in the weather, natural phenomena, or situations).
  + 空 (そら): sky.
  + 曇る (くもる): to become cloudy, overcast, or gloomy.
- Extended example: 空がにわかに暗くなり、大雨が降り始めた。(The sky suddenly grew dark, and heavy rain began to fall.) ＝ 急に空が暗くなり、大雨が降り始めた。
default.q.n3-tango-t16-mon4-30.why.0: (a) 「にわかに」 means “suddenly” or “abruptly.” It is commonly used to describe sudden changes in natural phenomena or weather and is an accurate synonym and replacement for 「急に」.
default.q.n3-tango-t16-mon4-30.why.1: (b) 「だんだん」means “gradually” or “little by little,” expressing a change that occurs progressively over time, in contrast to the suddenness of 「急に」.
default.q.n3-tango-t16-mon4-30.why.2: (c) 「やっと」 means “finally,” indicating that something was achieved after considerable effort, anticipation, or waiting; it does not describe something happening suddenly.
default.q.n3-tango-t16-mon4-30.why.3: (d) 「ついに」 means “at last, finally,” referring to an outcome after a long process, so it does not fit an immediate, unexpected change.
default.q.n3-tango-t16-mon5-31.verdict: The correct answer is 1: 言葉を交わして仲良くなった。
default.q.n3-tango-t16-mon5-31.explanation:
• Vocabulary: 交わす (かわす - KŌ) means to exchange something reciprocally between two or more parties, such as words, glances, greetings, or promises.
• Common expressions: 言葉を交わす (exchange words, converse), 挨拶を交わす (exchange greetings), 視線を交わす (exchange glances), 約束を交わす (make a promise with each other).
• Sentence translation 1: We talked with each other and became closer.
• Additional example: 朝、近所の人と笑顔で挨拶を交わした。(In the morning, I exchanged cheerful greetings with my neighbors.)
default.q.n3-tango-t16-mon5-31.why.0: (a) Correct because 交わす (かわす) means “to exchange” words, glances, greetings, and so on. The sentence correctly uses the familiar expression 「言葉を交わす」(exchange words, have a conversation).
default.q.n3-tango-t16-mon5-31.why.1: (b) Incorrect because the compound verb「取り交わす」means “to exchange” or “to conclude a contract”; the independent verb「交わす」is not used here in a complete sentence.
default.q.n3-tango-t16-mon5-31.why.2: (c) Incorrect. To say that someone avoids another person on the street or passes by them, use 「避ける」(さける - avoid) or 「すれ違う」(pass each other), not 「交わす」 with 「道」.
default.q.n3-tango-t16-mon5-31.why.3: (d) is incorrect because arranging or placing furniture in a room requires 「配置する」 (arrange), 「置く」 (put/place), or 「揃える」 (provide as a matching set), not 「交わす」.
default.q.n3-tango-t16-mon5-32.verdict: The correct answer is 1: この機械の操作は簡単だ。
default.q.n3-tango-t16-mon5-32.explanation:
• Vocabulary: 操作 (そうさ - THAO TÁC) means operating, controlling, or handling machinery and technical equipment; it can also mean manipulating data or markets.
• Common expressions: 機械を操作する (to operate machinery), パソコンの操作 (computer operation), リモコンで操作する (to control something with a remote control).
• Sentence 1 translation: Operating this machine is very simple.
• Distinction: 操作 (そうさ - operating machinery) differs from 捜査 (そうさ - criminal investigation), 手術 (しゅじゅつ - surgery), and 体操 (たいそう - physical exercise).

default.q.n3-tango-t16-mon5-32.why.0: (a) Correct because 操作 (そうさ) means operating or using machinery or equipment. The sentence correctly uses the phrase 「機械の操作」 (“operating machinery”).
default.q.n3-tango-t16-mon5-32.why.1: (b) Incorrect because exercising every morning requires 「体操」(たいそう - exercise) or 「運動」(うんどう), not 「操作」.
default.q.n3-tango-t16-mon5-32.why.2: (c) Incorrect because medical surgery is 「手術」(しゅじゅつ), while a criminal investigation is 「捜査」(そうさ). Although it has the same pronunciation as 操作, the latter means operation or manipulation. Since this context does not involve machinery, 「操作」is inappropriate.
default.q.n3-tango-t16-mon5-32.why.3: (d) Incorrect in this context: For a response or behavior that causes a problem, use 「対応」 (たいおう) or 「ミス / 行動」. 「操作」 is unnatural here because no specific system or device is involved.
default.q.n3-tango-t16-mon5-33.verdict: The correct answer is 1: 山の上に登って景色を眺めた。
default.q.n3-tango-t16-mon5-33.explanation:

default.q.n3-tango-t16-mon5-33.why.0: (a) Correct because 眺める (ながめる) means to look out over a broad space or view from a distance; it correctly forms the typical collocation 「景色を眺める」(to gaze at the scenery).
default.q.n3-tango-t16-mon5-33.why.1: (b) Incorrect because for a teacher’s lecture, one must use 「講義を聞く」 (“listen to a lecture”) or 「講義を受ける」 (“attend a lecture”), not 「眺める」.
default.q.n3-tango-t16-mon5-33.why.2: (c) Incorrect because music is perceived through hearing, so 「音楽を聴く / 聞く」 must be used; the visual verb 「眺める」 is inappropriate.
default.q.n3-tango-t16-mon5-33.why.3: (d) Incorrect because textbooks and other study materials should be read attentively, so use 「本を読む」 (read a book). 「眺める」 means to look at something absentmindedly and does not fit the purpose 「勉強する」.
default.q.n3-tango-t16-mon5-34.verdict: The correct answer is 1: 彼は常に冷静な判断をする。

default.q.n3-tango-t16-mon5-34.why.1: (b) Incorrect. To keep a room cool in temperature, use 「涼しく保つ」 (keep cool) or 「適温に保つ」 (keep at a suitable temperature). The psychological adjective 「冷静」 is not used for rooms.
default.q.n3-tango-t16-mon5-34.why.2: (c) Incorrect because when soup has cooled, use the verb 「冷める」(さめる, to cool down) or the adjective 「冷たい」(cold); 「冷静」is not used for food.

default.q.n3-tango-t16-mon5-35.verdict: The correct answer is 1: あっという間に時間が過ぎた。
default.q.n3-tango-t16-mon5-35.explanation:
• Vocabulary: あっという間に (あっというまに) originally conveys the idea of “in the brief time it takes to utter ‘ah,’” and is used to describe time passing extremely quickly or something being completed in the blink of an eye (in an instant, in the blink of an eye, before you know it).

default.q.n3-tango-t16-mon5-35.why.0: (a) Correct because あっという間に (in the blink of an eye, before one knows it) describes an extremely short amount of time passing. It correctly forms the classic expression あっという間に時間が過ぎる (time passes in the blink of an eye).
default.q.n3-tango-t16-mon5-35.why.1: (b) Incorrect. When asking someone to do something immediately, use 「今すぐ」(right now) or 「すぐに / 直ちに」(immediately); 「あっという間に」cannot be used in an imperative request.
default.q.n3-tango-t16-mon5-35.why.2: (c) Incorrect because to describe a person running at high speed, use 「速く走る」 (“run fast”); 「あっという間に走る」 is grammatically and collocationally incorrect.
default.q.n3-tango-t16-mon5-35.why.3: (d) Incorrect. To express that the weather suddenly changes to rain, use 「急に / 突然」 (suddenly), not 「あっという間に」 to modify a prediction about tomorrow’s rain.

default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon1-2.verdict: The correct answer is 1. ほしょうしょ (warranty card / warranty certificate).
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon1-2.explanation:

default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon1-3.verdict: The correct answer is 1. こころづかい (thoughtfulness, consideration).
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon1-3.explanation:
