  - 遣い is a noun derived from the verb 遣う (つかう). When it follows a noun, rendaku (連濁) changes it to づかい, as in 気遣い (きづかい), 心遣い (こころづかい), and 金遣い (かねづかい).
• Example: 温かいお心遣いをいただき、本当にありがとうございます。(Thank you very much for your warm and thoughtful consideration.)
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon1-3.why.0: (a) Correct. 心 has the kun-reading こころ, while 遣い undergoes rendaku, becoming づかい, forming こころづかい.
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon1-3.why.1: (b) Incorrect because 心 is read using its on-reading (しん) instead of its kun-reading (こころ).
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon1-3.why.2: (c) Incorrect because it omits the rendaku sound change in 遣い (it should be づかい, not つかい).
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon1-3.why.3: (d) Incorrect both because it uses the On-reading (しん) for 心 and omits the rendaku voicing in 遣い (つかい).
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon1-4.verdict: The correct answer is 1. ちんちゃく (calm, composed).
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon1-4.explanation:
• Sentence meaning: "He is always composed and calm."
• Kanji reading: 沈着 — composed, calm (often used in 冷静沈着 - れいせいちんちゃく: calm and collected).
  - 沈 has the on-reading ちん (as in 沈黙 ちんもく - silence, 沈没 ちんぼつ - sinking).
  - 着 has the on-reading ちゃく (as in 到着 とうちゃく - arrival, 定着 ていちゃく - becoming established).
• Example: どんな緊急事態でも、彼は沈着な態度を崩さない。(No matter what emergency he faces, he does not lose his composure.)
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon1-4.why.0: (a) Correct. 沈 has the on-reading ちん, and 着 has the on-reading ちゃく, so together they are read as ちんちゃく.
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon1-4.why.1: (b) Incorrect because the reading ちん of 沈 was mistakenly changed to the voiced sound じん.
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon1-4.why.2: (c) Incorrect because the reading ちゃく of 着 has been mistaken for the voiced reading じゃく.
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon1-4.why.3: (d) Incorrect because 沈 (ちん) was confused with the reading しん, which is easily confused with kanji such as 深, 慎, and 新.
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon1-5.verdict: The correct answer is 1. ゆうえき (useful, beneficial).
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon1-5.explanation:
• Meaning: “This book is extremely useful.”
• On’yomi: 有益 (HỮU ÍCH) — useful, beneficial.
  - 有 (HỮU) commonly has the on-reading ゆう (as in 有名 ゆうめい — famous, 有料 ゆうりょう — fee-based, 有効 ゆうこう — valid/effective).
  - 益 (ÍCH) has the on-reading えき (as in 利益 りえき — benefit/profit, 有益 ゆうえき — useful/beneficial).
• Example: 週末のセミナーで大変有益な情報を得ることができた。(I was able to obtain very useful information at the weekend seminar.)
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon1-5.why.0: (a) Correct. 有 is read with the on-reading ゆう, and 益 with the on-reading えき, giving ゆうえき.
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon1-5.why.1: (b) Incorrect because it confuses the reading of 益 (えき) with the less common reading やく, as in ご利益 (ごりやく).
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon1-5.why.2: (c) Incorrect because 有 (HỮU) is missing its long vowel (it should be ゆう, not ゆ).
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon1-5.why.3: (d) Both are incorrect because the long vowel in 有 is missing and 益 has the wrong on-yomi.
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon1-6.verdict: The correct answer is 1. かかさず (without missing anything, regularly and without fail).
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon1-6.explanation:
• Sentence meaning: “She goes jogging every morning without missing a single day.”
• Kanji reading: 欠かさず: regularly, without missing a day.
  - 欠 in 欠く (かく: to lack, chip, or damage); the negative adverbial form 欠かさず (かかさず) means “without missing” or “consistently.”
  - The on-reading of 欠 is けつ (e.g., 欠席 けっせき: absence; 欠点 けってん: fault, shortcoming).
• Example: 祖父は毎日の散歩を欠かさず続けている。(My grandfather continues his daily walks without missing a day.)
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon1-6.why.0: (a) Correct. The kanji 欠 is read か(く) in the verb 欠く, and its negative conjunctive form is 欠かさず (かかさず).
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon1-6.why.1: (b) Incorrect because the on- and kun-readings have been combined incorrectly, producing a meaningless word.
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon1-6.why.2: (c) Incorrect because it directly attaches the on-reading けつ of 欠 to the verb's grammatical ending.
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon1-6.why.3: (d) Incorrect because Japanese words do not begin with a small っ.
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon1-7.verdict: The correct answer is 1. すきとおって (transparent, crystal clear).
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon1-7.explanation:
• Sentence meaning: "The river water is crystal clear (clear enough to see the bottom)."
• Related kanji-based vocabulary: 透き通って (clear, transparent).
  - 透 has the kun-readings す(く) / す(かす) / す(ける) -> 透き (すき).
  - 通 has the kun-reading とお(る) -> 通って (とおって).
  - The compound verb 透き通る (すきとおる) retains the とおる sound (it does not become どおる through sequential voicing), and changes to 透き通って (すきとおって) in the te-form.
• Example: 透き通るような青い海が目の前に広がっていた。(A crystal-clear blue sea stretched out before me.)
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon1-7.why.0: (a) Correct. 透き is read as すき, and 通って is the te-form of 通る, read as とおって, giving すきとおって.
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon1-7.why.1: (b) Incorrect because 通る does not undergo rendaku in this compound; it remains とおる, not どおる.
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon1-7.why.2: (c) Incorrect because the te-form of the godan verb 通る (とおる) must have a geminate consonant, とおって, not とおて.
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon1-7.why.3: (d) Incorrect because both the rendaku change is wrong (ど) and the sokuon is missing when forming the te-form (て instead of って).
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon1-8.verdict: The correct answer is 1. せんもんか (expert).
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon1-8.explanation:
• Sentence meaning: "He is an expert in this field."
• Kanji etymology: 専門家 (SEN-MON-KA) — specialist, expert.
  - 専 (SEN) has the on-reading せん (as in 専門 せんもん, 専用 せんよう — for exclusive use, 専攻 せんこう — major).
  - 門 (MON) has the on-reading もん (as in 専門 せんもん, 部門 ぶもん — department/field).
  - 家 (KA), when used as a suffix for someone’s profession or area of expertise, is read with the on-reading か (as in 専門家 せんもんか — expert, 政治家 せいじか — politician, 画家 がか — painter).
• Example: 専門家の意見を聞いてから判断したほうがいい。(It is better to make a decision after hearing an expert’s opinion.)
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon1-8.why.0: (a) Correct. 専 is read せん, 門 is read もん, and 家 is read か, giving せんもんか.
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon1-8.why.1: (b) Incorrect because the suffix for a professional or specialist is read か, not け. The reading け is commonly used for a family or clan, as in 徳川家 とくがわけ.
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon1-8.why.2: (c) Incorrect because 専 has the on-reading せん and does not undergo voicing to become ぜん.
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon1-8.why.3: (d) Both are incorrect: 専 is read as ぜん and 家 is read as け.
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon2-9.verdict: The correct answer is 1. 宿題 (homework).
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon2-9.explanation:
Meaning: I forgot to do my homework, so the teacher scolded me.
- 宿題: 宿 (lodging, staying) + 題 (topic, problem), meaning an assignment given to be completed at home.
- Related word: 出題 (しゅつだい: to set or prepare an exam question).
- Example: 毎日の宿題をちゃんとやってください。(Please do your homework properly every day.)
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon2-9.why.0: (a) 宿題: Correct. This is the standard kanji for しゅくだい, meaning homework.
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon2-9.why.1: (b) 祝題: Incorrect. The 祝 is the character in 祝う (to celebrate), so it cannot be combined to form this word.
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon2-9.why.2: (c) 縮題: Incorrect because 縮 is the character in 縮む, meaning to shrink or become smaller, and does not form this word.
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon2-9.why.3: (d) 出題: This word is read as しゅつだい and means “to set an exam” or “to pose a question”; it is not read as しゅくだい.
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon2-10.verdict: The correct answer is 2. 機能 (function, feature).
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon2-10.explanation:
Sentence translation: Try out the functions/features of the new camera.
- 機能: Consists of 機 (mechanism, machine) and 能 (ability, capacity), referring to the functions or operating features of machines, devices, or body parts.
- Note: Distinguish it from the homophone 昨日 (きのう: yesterday).
- Example: このスマートフォンには多くの便利な機能がついている。(This smartphone has many convenient features.)
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon2-10.why.0: (a) 幾能: The kanji 幾 is incorrect; it appears in words such as 幾つ and 幾何学 and does not form a meaningful word here.
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon2-10.why.1: (b) 機能: Correct. This is the standard kanji for きのう, meaning function or feature.
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon2-10.why.2: (c) 帰能: Incorrect. The 帰 is the character in 帰る (to return), and this combination does not form a meaningful word.
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon2-10.why.3: (d) 気能: Incorrect. The kanji 気, as in 気分 and 気持ち, does not form a meaningful word here.
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon2-11.verdict: The correct answer is 2. 笑顔 (a smiling expression, smile).
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon2-11.explanation:
Sentence translation: She always keeps a smile on her face.
- 笑顔: Made up of 笑 (to laugh, smile) and 顔 (face), meaning a smiling expression or radiant smile.
- Common expressions: 笑顔を絶やさない (always keep smiling), 笑顔を見せる (show a smile).
- Example: 子供たちの笑顔を見て元気づけられた。(Seeing the children's smiles lifted my spirits.)
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon2-11.why.0: (a) 笑顔: The correct kanji for えがお (smile, smiling face).
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon2-11.why.1: (b) 笑顔: Correct. This is the standard kanji for えがお and means a smiling facial expression or bright smile.
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon2-11.why.2: (c) 咲顔 uses the wrong character, 咲, as in 咲く (for flowers blooming). It is not used to write えがお in standard Japanese.
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon2-11.why.3: (d) 喜顔: Incorrect. The kanji 喜 means joy, as in 喜ぶ; Japanese does not use 喜顔 for えがお.
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon2-12.verdict: The correct answer is 1. 空気 (air).
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon2-12.explanation:
- Sentence translation: Ventilate the room / change the air.
- 空気 (air): Made up of 空 (sky, emptiness) and 気 (air, atmosphere, spirit), it means the air or atmosphere around us.
- Common expressions: 空気を入(れ)換える (to change the air, ventilate), 空気を読む (to read the atmosphere and understand what others mean).
- Example: 窓を開けて部屋の空気を入れ換えた。(I opened the window to ventilate the room.)
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon2-12.why.0: (a) 空気: Correct. This is the standard kanji for くうき and means air or atmosphere.
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon2-12.why.1: (b) 空器: Incorrect kanji. 器 is used in 食器 and 器具, meaning a utensil or tool; its on-reading is き, but the meaning is wrong here.
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon2-12.why.2: (c) 空季: Incorrect kanji. 季 in 季節 means season; its on-reading is き, but the meaning is incorrect here.
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon2-12.why.3: (d) 空規: Incorrect because 規 is the character in 規則, meaning rule; its on-reading is き, but the meaning is wrong here.
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon2-13.verdict: The correct answer is 3. 規則 (RULE: rule, regulation).
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon2-13.explanation:
Sentence translation: Follow the traffic rules.
- 規則: Consists of 規 (rules, standards) and 則 (rules, regulations), and means rules, regulations, or laws. 交通規則 (こうつうきそく) is equivalent to 交通ルール (traffic rules).
- Distinguishing words containing 規 (all read き):
  + 規制 (きせい): regulation, control, restriction (e.g., 交通規制: traffic control/restrictions).
  + 規律 (きりつ): discipline, order.
  + 規約 (きやく): agreement, common regulations.
- Example: 学校の規則をしっかり守ってください。(Please strictly follow the school's rules.)
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon2-13.why.0: (a) 規制: Read as きせい, meaning regulation, control/restriction.
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon2-13.why.1: (b) 規律 (QUY LUẬT): Read as きりつ, meaning discipline, order.
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon2-13.why.2: (c) 規則: Correct. This is the standard kanji spelling of きそく, meaning rules or regulations (交通規則: traffic regulations).
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon2-13.why.3: (d) 規約: Read as きやく, meaning rules, regulations.
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon2-14.verdict: The correct answer is 1. 詳細 (details, particulars).
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon2-14.explanation:
Sentence meaning: Please explain the matter in detail.
- 詳細 (しょうさい): combines 詳 (しょう, as in 詳しい くわしい — detailed, clear) with 細 (さい, as in 細かい こまかい — fine, minute), meaning detailed, thorough, or specific.
- This word can be used as a noun or as a na-adjective (詳細なデータ — detailed data).
- Example: 旅行の計画について、詳細が決まったら連絡します。(I will contact you once the details of the travel plan have been finalized.)
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon2-14.why.0: (a) 詳細: Correct. This is the standard kanji for しょうさい, meaning details or particulars.
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon2-14.why.1: (b) 詳載: Incorrect because 載 is the wrong kanji (as in 掲載 and 載る, meaning to publish or record); it is not used in しょうさい.
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon2-14.why.2: (c) 少細: Incorrect; 少 means “few” and does not form a meaningful word here.
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon2-14.why.3: (d) 小細: Incorrectly uses 小 (SMALL), so it does not form the word しょうさい (easily confused with 小細工 こざいく).
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon3-15.explanation:
- Sentence meaning: "Her singing voice is truly beautiful."
- Related kanji-based vocabulary:
  + 彼女: she, girlfriend
  + 歌声: singing voice
  + 実に: truly, really
  + 美しい: beautiful
- Key point: The pattern 「実に ＋ adjective」is used for exclamation and emphasizes a high degree or outstanding quality in a formal, expressive style.
- Example: 富士山からの景色は実に素晴らしい。(The view from Mount Fuji is truly wonderful.)
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon3-15.why.0: (a) 実に (“indeed, truly”): This adverb emphasizes a high degree and carries an exclamatory nuance (“the singing voice is truly beautiful”), making it a very natural combination with 美しい.
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon3-15.why.1: (b) 実に (a duplicated choice in the question): has a meaning similar to choice 1, but the officially designated answer position is 1.
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon3-15.why.2: (c) まさに (exactly, precisely): used to emphasize authenticity or an exact moment, as in まさにその通り (that is exactly right). It is not used as an adverb modifying the degree of 美しい.
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon3-15.why.3: (d) まったく (completely): usually used with a negative sentence (まったく〜ない: not at all) or to express dissatisfaction (まったく困ったものだ), so it is unsuitable for praising a singing voice.
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon3-16.verdict: The correct answer is 1 (ぎりぎり).
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon3-16.explanation:
- Sentence translation: “I arrived just in time for the appointment.”
- Related kanji readings:
  + 約束: appointment, promise.
  + 時間: time.
  + 間に合う: be in time.
- Important N3 onomatopoeia and mimetic words:
  + ぎりぎり: just in time, by a narrow margin (ぎりぎりで合格した: passed by a narrow margin).
  + ぐらぐら: wobble, shake (地震で家がぐらぐら揺れた: the house shook violently in the earthquake).
  + ごろごろ: roll around; lounge idly (休日は家でごろごろしている: I lounge around at home on my days off).
  + がらがら: nearly empty (平日なので電車はがらがらだ: the train is nearly empty because it is a weekday).
- Example: ぎりぎり終電に間に合いました。 (I just barely caught the last train.)
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon3-16.why.0: (a) ぎりぎり (“just in time,” “at the last moment”): Combines with 間に合う to form the very common fixed expression 「ぎりぎり間に合う」 (“to make it just in time”), making it completely accurate.
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon3-16.why.1: (b) ぐらぐら (wobbling, shaking): describes something unstable that sways or shakes, such as a loose tooth or ground shaking during an earthquake; it is not used with time.
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon3-16.why.2: (c) ごろごろ (rolling around, lounging idly, thunder rumbling): it is not used to describe being on time for an appointment.
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon3-16.why.3: (d) がらがら (“completely empty,” “hoarse”): describes an empty movie theater or bus, or a hoarse voice, so it does not fit the context.
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon3-17.explanation:
- Meaning: “This question looks easier than expected.”
- Kanji:
  + 問題: question, problem
  + 案外: unexpectedly, contrary to expectations
  + 簡単: simple, easy
- Difference between 案外 and 意外:
  + 案外 functions independently as an adverb and directly modifies an adjective or verb (案外簡単だ, 案外おいしい).
  + 意外 is a na-adjective; to modify an adjective or verb adverbially, it must take the form 「意外に / 意外と」.
- Example: 彼の料理は案外おいしかった。(His cooking was unexpectedly delicious.)
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon3-17.why.0: (a) 案外 (“unexpectedly, contrary to expectations”): an adverb that directly modifies 簡単そうだ, indicating a result or state different from what was initially expected.
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon3-17.why.1: (b) 意外 means unexpected or contrary to expectations. It is a na-adjective and needs a particle, becoming 「意外に」or 「意外と」when modifying 簡単そうだ, so using it alone is grammatically incomplete.
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon3-17.why.2: (c) 存外 (“beyond expectation”) has a literary or formal tone and is unsuitable for an ordinary conversational sentence at the N3 level.
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon3-17.why.3: (d) 例外 (exception): a noun referring to an individual case outside the general rule; it does not function as an adverb modifying an adjective.
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon3-18.explanation:
- Meaning: "His explanation is extremely / exceptionally easy to understand."
- Related vocabulary and kanji readings:
  + 説明 (せつめい): explanation, description
  + 極めて (きわめて): extremely, exceptionally
  + 極端 (きょくたん): extreme
  + 絶対 (ぜったい): absolute, absolutely
- Key point:
  + 「極めて」 is a formal adverb (equivalent to とても / 非常に), typically modifying adjectives expressing a high degree (極めて重要: extremely important, 極めて優秀: exceptionally excellent).
- Example: その計画は極めて重要である。(That plan is extremely important.)
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon3-18.why.0: (a) 極めて (extremely, exceedingly): A formal adverb indicating a very high degree, it combines naturally with わかりやすい to praise something as exceptionally clear and easy to understand.
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon3-18.why.1: (b) 極端に (extremely, excessively): conveys a negative or overly unbalanced sense, as in 極端に偏る (be extremely biased); it is not used to praise a clear explanation.
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon3-18.why.2: (c) 絶対に (absolutely, definitely) is used to express certainty or strong determination (e.g., 絶対に諦めない — I will never give up), and is not an adverb indicating the degree of わかりやすい.
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon3-18.why.3: (d) 大いに (“very much, greatly”): It commonly modifies verbs expressing enjoyment, praise, or expectation, such as 大いに楽しむ and 大いに役立つ. It does not normally modify the adjective わかりやすい.
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon3-19.explanation:
- Translation: "I installed software on the new computer."
- Kanji and vocabulary:
  + 新しい: new
  + パソコン: personal computer
- Common IT loanwords in katakana:
  + ソフト (Software): software
  + ハード (Hardware): hardware
  + インストールする (Install): to install software or an application
  + アンインストールする (Uninstall): to uninstall
- Example: ウイルス対策ソフトをインストールした。(I installed antivirus software.)
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon3-19.why.0: (a) ソフト (software, shortened from ソフトウェア): combines with インストールする to form the correct computing expression ソフトをインストールする (to install software).
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon3-19.why.1: (b) ハード (hardware - ハードウェア): refers to physical components and machines, so it cannot be used with the action インストール (to install software).
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon3-19.why.2: (c) コード (code, electrical cable) is not used with the action インストール.
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon3-19.why.3: (d) モード (mode, operating method) is commonly used with the verb 切り替える (switch modes), not with インストール.
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon3-20.explanation:
- Meaning: “He insisted on maintaining his position to the very end, despite the opposition.”
- Kanji and vocabulary:
  + 自分: oneself
  + 意見: opinion, view
  + 押し通す: to insist on something to the end, push something through (おしとおす)
- Verbs with 〜通す (to continue doing something to the end / throughout):
  + 押し通す (おしとおす): to insist on or push through an opinion, claim, or demand (意見/主張/要求を押し通す)
  + やり通す (やりとおす): to carry something through without giving up halfway
  + 嘘をつき通す (うそをつきとおす): to keep lying successfully from beginning to end
- Example: 反対意見もあったが、彼は自分の企画を押し通した。(Although there were opposing opinions, he pushed his project through to the end.)
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon3-20.why.0: (a) 主張し (“asserting,” “insisting”): 「主張する」 is a Group 3 verb and cannot be directly combined with 「〜通す」 to form a grammatically correct compound verb.
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon3-20.why.1: (b) 言い (say): 「言い通す」 means to keep saying something from beginning to end, such as stubbornly maintaining a lie; it does not form an expression meaning to defend one's position forcefully, as 押し通す does.
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon3-20.why.2: (c) 押し (to push): Combined with 通す, it forms the compound verb 「押し通す」(おしとおす). The phrase 「自分の意見を押し通す」means to insist on or force through one's own opinion despite opposition from others.
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon3-20.why.3: (d) 引き (pull): There is no compound verb 「引き通す」that fits the context of expressing an opinion.
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon3-21.explanation:
- Meaning: "These shoes feel extremely comfortable on my feet."
- Sino-Japanese vocabulary:
  + 靴 (NGOA): shoes (くつ)
  + 履き心地: the feel of wearing shoes (はきごこち)
  + 抜群: outstanding, exceptional (ばつぐん)
  + 当然: natural, of course
  + 突然: sudden, suddenly
  + 自然: natural, naturally
- Extended expressions with 〜心地:
  + 履き心地: the feel of wearing shoes
  + 着心地: the feel of wearing clothes (きごこち)
  + 居心地: how comfortable one feels in a place (いごこち)
- Example: 彼女はスタイルが抜群に良い。(She has an exceptionally good figure.)
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon3-21.why.0: (a) 抜群に means “exceptionally, outstandingly, extremely.” It is an adverb used to praise something as far above the ordinary; 「抜群にいい」 describes shoes that feel exceptionally comfortable.
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon3-21.why.1: (b) 当然に means “naturally” or “of course” and is not used as an adverb expressing the degree of comfort when evaluating how shoes feel.
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon3-21.why.2: (c) 突然に (suddenly, unexpectedly): describes something happening abruptly in time; it is unrelated to product quality.
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon3-21.why.3: (d) 自然に means “naturally,” describing an unforced action; it is not used to express that the wearing comfort of 履き心地 is exceptionally good.
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon3-22.explanation:
- Meaning: The development of the new product is progressing very smoothly.
- Kanji vocabulary:
  + 新製品: new product
  + 開発: development, research and development
  + 順調: smooth, going well
  + 順序: order, sequence
  + 秩序: order, discipline
- Common workplace expressions:
  + 順調に進む (progress smoothly)
  + 順調に回復する (recover smoothly)
- Example: 手術後の経過は順調です。(Recovery after the surgery is progressing smoothly.)
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon3-22.why.0: (a) 順調 (smoothly, favorably): A na-adjective that combines with the particle に to form 「順調に進む」(progress smoothly), which is entirely appropriate for the progress of a project.
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon3-22.why.1: (b) 調子 (condition, form): is a noun commonly used in the pattern 「調子がいい/悪い」; it does not directly combine as 「調子に進む」.
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon3-22.why.2: (c) 順序 (“order,” “sequence”): A noun referring to the steps in a procedure, commonly used in 「順序よく」 or 「順序に従って」; it is not used to refer to work progress.
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon3-22.why.3: (d) 秩序 (order, discipline) is a noun referring to social order or discipline, as in 秩序を守る (maintain order). It is unrelated to a product’s progress or development.
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon3-23.explanation:
- Meaning: "She always treated me with a very polite and courteous attitude."
- On-reading and kanji notes:
  + 態度: attitude, manner
  + 接する: to come into contact with, treat, attend to (せっする)
  + 丁寧: polite, courteous, careful (ていねい)
  + 親切: kind, helpful (しんせつ)
  + 公平: fair
  + 平等: equal, equality
- Distinction:
  + 「丁寧な態度」: a polite, courteous, and appropriate attitude in communication and interactions.
  + 「親切」: a kind, helpful personality; often used in expressions such as 親切にする or 親切に教えてくれる.
- Example: 店員はお客さんに丁寧な言葉遣いで対応した。(The store clerk attended to the customer using very polite language.)
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon3-23.why.0: (a) 公平 (“fair, impartial”): Used when making a judgment or evaluation without bias, as in 公平な判断. It does not describe a polite, considerate manner of treating others.
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon3-23.why.1: (b) 平等 means “equality” and is used for rights and social status, as in 男女平等; it is not used as a modifier for everyday interpersonal attitudes.
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon3-23.why.2: (c) 親切 (kind, helpful) generally refers to kindness or helping others, as in 親切にする. When describing a courteous, polite, and respectful manner, 丁寧な態度 is the most accurate expression.
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon3-23.why.3: (d) 丁寧 (polite, courteous, considerate): The phrase「丁寧な態度で接する」(treat someone with a polite, courteous attitude) is the most natural and accurate collocation.
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon3-24.explanation:
- Sentence translation: "The nature in this area is rich and abundant."
- Kanji and vocabulary:
  + 地域: area, region.
  + 自然: nature, natural environment.
  + 豊か: abundant, rich, prosperous (ゆたか).
  + 天然: natural, non-artificial.
- Fixed expressions to remember:
  + 自然が豊か: rich in nature, with beautiful natural surroundings.
  + 資源が豊か: rich in resources.
- Difference between 自然 and 天然:
  + 自然: the natural environment in general, such as plants, forests, mountains, rivers, and lakes.
  + 天然: a natural quality, in contrast to 人工 (artificial), as in 天然水 (natural mineral water) and 天然温泉 (natural hot spring).
- Example: 私の故郷は山に囲まれ、自然が豊かな場所です。(My hometown is surrounded by mountains and is rich in nature.)
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon3-24.why.0: (a) 自然 (“nature, natural”): it forms the fixed expression 「自然が豊か」 (“rich in nature”) to describe the vegetation and scenery of an area.
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon3-24.why.1: (b) 天然 means “natural” and is commonly used attributively before a noun to describe products or resources that are not artificially made, such as 天然ガス and 天然水. It is not used in the expression 「天然が豊か」.
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon3-24.why.2: (c) 公然 (“openly, publicly”): means openly in front of everyone (e.g., 公然の秘密, an open secret); it is unrelated to this context.
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon3-24.why.3: (d) 必然 (inevitability, necessity): refers to something that must occur according to a закономерность, as in 必然的な結果 (an inevitable result), so it does not fit here.
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon3-25.explanation:
- Meaning: "I will distribute the materials for tomorrow's meeting."
- Kanji and vocabulary:
  + 会議: meeting
  + 資料: materials, handouts (しりょう)
  + 配る: distribute (くばる)
  + 材料: raw materials, ingredients (ざいりょう)
  + 原料: raw material (げんりょう)
  + 料金: fee, charge (りょうきん)
- Distinguishing words containing 料:
  + 資料: documents, information, or charts used for study and meetings.
  + 材料: materials whose physical form is recognizable, such as meat or fish for cooking and wood for furniture.
  + 原料: raw materials whose properties are changed during the production of a finished product, such as barley for beer or crude oil for plastic.
- Example: 会議が始まる前に、参加者に資料を配ってください。 (Please distribute the materials to the participants before the meeting begins.)
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon3-25.why.0: (a) 資料 (materials/documents): Written materials or documents containing information for a meeting. Combining it with 配る to form 「資料を配る」(hand out the materials) is completely correct.
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon3-25.why.1: (b) 材料: Means ingredients, materials, or supplies, such as in 料理の材料. It is not used for a meeting document.
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon3-25.why.2: (c) 原料 (raw material) refers to materials used in industrial production (such as ビールの原料), not to a meeting.
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon3-25.why.3: (d) 料金 (fee, charge): money paid for a service, such as 電気料金 (electricity charges), and cannot be used to mean “to issue” in a meeting.
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon4-26.verdict: Choice 1 (あわてず) is correct because it means remaining calm and not becoming flustered or panicked.
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon4-26.explanation:
• Sentence translation: He always handles situations calmly.
• Vocabulary:
  - 冷静（れいせい）: calm, composed, able to remain calm in difficult situations.
  - 対処（たいしょ）: to deal with, handle, or resolve a situation.
  - 慌てる（あわてる）: to panic, become flustered, or lose one's composure (negative form: あわてず = without panicking, calmly).
• Example: どんなトラブルが起きても、冷静に（＝あわてず）行動することが大切だ。(No matter what trouble occurs, it is important to act calmly / without panicking.)
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon4-26.why.0: (a) 「あわてず」 comes from the verb 「慌てる」（あわてる: to panic, become flustered） in its negative form, meaning “without panicking or becoming flustered.” In this context, it naturally has the same meaning as and can replace 「冷静に」（calmly, composedly） when dealing with a problem.
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon4-26.why.1: (b) 「いそいで」（急いで） means “hurriedly” or “urgently,” emphasizing the speed of an action rather than a calm and composed mental state.
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon4-26.why.2: (c) 「のんびり」 means "leisurely, relaxed, carefree," expressing an untroubled attitude that differs from calmly and seriously dealing with a situation.
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon4-26.why.3: (d) 「きびしく」（厳しく）means “strictly” or “severely,” describing a disciplined, firm attitude, not calmness.
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon4-27.verdict: Choice 1 (あじがしない) is correct because it describes food that is very bland, with almost no perceptible taste, equivalent to 「うすい」.
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon4-27.explanation:
• Translation of the original sentence: This soup is too bland.
• Vocabulary & kanji readings:
  - 薄い（BẠC - うすい）: bland (taste), thin (thickness), pale/dilute (color or density).
  - 濃い（NỒNG - こい）: strong, thick, rich (the opposite of 薄い).
  - 味（VỊ - あじ）: taste, flavor.
• N3 note: When 薄い is used for food or drinks such as tea, soup, or broth, it means “bland” or “watery.” あじがしない (“has little or no taste”) is the closest expression for a lack of flavor.
• Example: お湯を入れすぎて、スープの味がうすくなってしまった（＝あまり味がしない）。(I added too much hot water, so the soup became too bland.)
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon4-27.why.0: (a) 「あじがしない」 (味がしない) means “has no taste” or “is very bland,” correctly describing food with little flavor and corresponding to 「うすい」 (薄い: bland, weak) when tasting food or soup.
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon4-27.why.1: (b) 「あじがこい」（味が濃い） means “strongly flavored” or “salty/strong-tasting,” making it the complete antonym of 「うすい」.
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon4-27.why.2: (c) 「あまい」（甘い）means “sweet,” referring to a specific taste; it does not mean “bland.”
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon4-27.why.3: (d) 「からい」（辛い） means “spicy” or “sharply salty,” referring specifically to those tastes; it is not equivalent to “bland.”
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon4-28.verdict: Choice 1 (ほんをかくひと) is correct because 「作家」 refers to a writer or author who writes books or stories.
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon4-28.explanation:
• Meaning of the original sentence: She is a famous writer.
• Vocabulary and kanji meanings:
  - 作家（さっか）: author, writer, creator of works, especially books and novels.
  - 有名（ゆうめい）: famous.
  - 著書（ちょしょ）: a published work, book.
• Other occupation nouns ending in 「家」:
  - 芸術家（げいじゅつか）: artist
  - 画家（がか）: painter
  - 音楽家（おんがくか）: musician
  - 建築家（けんちくか）: architect
• Illustrative example: 彼は将来、小説を出版して有名な作家（＝本を書く人）になりたいと思っている。(He hopes to publish a novel in the future and become a famous writer.)
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon4-28.why.0: (a) 「ほんをかくひと」（本を書く人）means “a person who writes books,” which precisely defines「作家」(a writer or author of literary works, books, or articles).
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon4-28.why.1: (b) 「えをかくひと」（絵を描く人） means “a person who draws pictures,” corresponding to 「画家」（がか, painter） or 「イラストレーター」.
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon4-28.why.2: (c) 「うたをうたうひと」（歌を歌う人） means “a person who sings,” corresponding to 「歌手」（かしゅ—singer）.
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon4-28.why.3: (d) 「おどるひと」（踊る人）means “a person who dances,” corresponding to 「ダンサー」or 「舞踏家」（ぶとうか - dancer）.
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon4-29.verdict: Choice 3 (しゅうかん) is correct because 「ルーティン」(routine) is synonymous with 「習慣」, referring to daily habits or routines.
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon4-29.explanation:
• Sentence translation: Complete the morning routine.
• Vocabulary:
  - ルーティン (routine): a daily habit or a series of repeated actions performed according to a regular schedule.
  - 習慣 (しゅうかん): habit, customary way of life.
  - こなす（熟す）: to complete, handle skillfully, or finish successfully.
  - 毎朝 (まいあさ): every morning.
• Example: 朝起きてからコップ1杯の水を飲むのが、私の毎日のルーティン（＝習慣）です。(Drinking a glass of water after waking up is my daily routine (= habit).)
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon4-29.why.0: (a) 「きまり」（決まり） means “rule,” “regulation,” or “convention,” referring to something agreed upon or established that must be followed; it does not mean a personal daily habit.
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon4-29.why.1: (b) 「きそく」（規則） means “rule” or “regulation,” referring to requirements that must be followed, such as company or school rules.
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon4-29.why.2: (c) 「しゅうかん」(習慣) means “habit, custom,” referring to repeated actions that become part of one’s daily routine. It is the closest equivalent and best replacement for 「ルーティン」(routine).
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon4-29.why.3: (d) 「よてい」（予定） means “plan, schedule” and refers to something planned in advance; it does not necessarily refer to activities repeated every day as a habit.
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon4-30.verdict: Choice 1 (すぐに) is correct because 「たちまち」means “immediately, in an instant,” describing a change that occurs very quickly.
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon4-30.explanation:
• Sentence translation: The rain stopped in an instant.
• Vocabulary:
  - たちまち（忽ち）: in an instant, immediately, before long (describing an extremely rapid change of state).
  - 雨がやむ（あめがやむ）: the rain stops.
• Note on distinguishing adverbs of time:
  - たちまち ＝ すぐに / あっという間に: in the blink of an eye, immediately (emphasizing an extremely rapid change).
  - とうとう / ついに: finally, at last (emphasizing a result after a long period of waiting or a series of events).
• Example: 新発売のお菓子は、人気があってたちまち（＝すぐに）売り切れた。(The newly released snack was so popular that it sold out immediately.)
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon4-30.why.0: (a) 「すぐに」means "immediately" or "at once," making it an exact replacement for 「たちまち」(忽ち: in an instant, immediately) to describe the rain stopping very quickly.
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon4-30.why.1: (b) 「ゆっくり」 means slowly, leisurely, or unhurriedly, which is the opposite of the sudden, rapid progression expressed by 「たちまち」.
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon4-30.why.2: (c) 「とうとう」 means “finally” or “in the end,” and is commonly used for a result that occurs after a long process, often with a negative or unavoidable nuance.
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon4-30.why.3: (d) 「ついに」（遂に）means “finally,” and is generally used when something expected or pursued over a long period eventually produces a result.
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon5-31.verdict: The correct answer is 1: 荷物を部屋に運び入れる。
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon5-31.explanation:
- 運び入れる【はこびいれる】(VẬN NHẬP): carry or move inside; transport objects or goods from outside into a specific enclosed space such as a room, warehouse, or building.
- Meaning of the correct sentence: 荷物を部屋に運び入れる。(I carry the luggage into the room.)
- Extended example: 新しい家具をリビングに運び入れた。(We moved the new furniture into the living room.)
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon5-31.why.0: (a) Correct. 「運び入れる」means to carry or move something from outside into a specific space. In this context, using it for moving luggage into the room is completely natural and accurate.
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon5-31.why.1: (b) Incorrect. For sending a car to be repaired, use 「車を修理に出す」(send the car for repair), not 「運び入れる」.
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon5-31.why.2: (c) Incorrect. Depositing or putting money into a bank is usually expressed as 「お金を銀行に預ける」 (deposit money) or 「入金する」. 「運び入れる」 is not used for this ordinary action.
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon5-31.why.3: (d) Incorrect. To return a book to the library, say 「本を図書館に返す」. To bring a book to the library, ordinarily say 「本を図書館に持っていく」.
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon5-32.verdict: The correct answer is 1: 今回の企画は大成功だった。
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon5-32.explanation:
- 企画【きかく】: plan, project, proposal for organizing a program or event (commonly used in work, media, and events when planning and implementing a specific program or project).
- Meaning of the correct sentence: 今回の企画は大成功だった。(This project/program was a great success.)
- Extended example: 新商品の販売企画を立てる。(To draw up a sales plan for a new product line.)
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon5-32.why.0: (a) Correct. 「企画」 means a plan or a project/program that has been conceived. Combined with 「大成功だった」 (“was a great success”), it creates a very natural and accurate context.
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon5-32.why.1: (b) Incorrect. When traveling according to a friend’s suggestion or plan, 「計画」 (“plan”) or 「提案」 (“proposal”) is usually used. 「企画」 generally refers to an organized project, event, or large-scale undertaking.
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon5-32.why.2: (c) Incorrect. Room cleaning cannot be used with 「企画」; to say “clean the corners of the room,” use 「部屋の隅 (すみ) を掃除する」, or simply 「部屋の掃除をする」.
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon5-32.why.3: (d) Incorrect. To make a meal plan, use 「料理の献立 (こんだて) を作る」, or use 「レシピを作る」 to create a recipe, not 「企画」.
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon5-33.verdict: The correct answer is 1: 彼女は素晴らしい才能を発揮した。
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon5-33.explanation:
- 発揮【はっき】: to demonstrate or make full use of (usually used with nouns describing inherent abilities, such as 才能 (talent), 実力 (ability), 能力 (capability), and リーダーシップ (leadership)).
- Correct sentence: 彼女は素晴らしい才能を発揮した。(She demonstrated her outstanding talent.)
- Additional example: 試合で日頃の練習の成果を十分に発揮できた。(I was able to fully demonstrate the results of my daily practice in the match.)
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon5-33.why.0: (a) Correct. 「才能を発揮する」(to demonstrate one’s talent) is an especially standard and common collocation.
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon5-33.why.1: (b) Incorrect. For a vehicle traveling at high speed, use 「スピードを出す」(to speed up / drive fast), not 「スピードを発揮する」.
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon5-33.why.2: (c) Incorrect. Weather cannot be used with 「発揮する」; to say that the weather is good or bad, use 「天気がいい / 悪い」.
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon5-33.why.3: (d) Incorrect. To describe cleaning a room thoroughly or finishing something all at once, adverbs such as 「きれいに」 (“cleanly”) or 「一気に」 (“in one go”) are used; 「発揮して」 cannot be used.
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon5-34.verdict: The correct answer is 1: 彼は常に前向きな考え方をする。
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon5-34.explanation:
- 前向き【まえむき】: positive, optimistic, forward-looking. It is often used to describe an attitude, way of thinking, or approach, as in 前向きな姿勢 (a positive attitude) and 前向きに検討する (consider positively).
- Meaning of the correct sentence: 彼は常に前向きな考え方をする。(He always has a positive way of thinking.)
- Extended example: 失敗しても落ち込まず、前向きに取り組もう。(Even if we fail, let's not get discouraged; let's keep working positively.)
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon5-34.why.0: (a) Correct.「前向きな考え方」(a positive/optimistic way of thinking) is the standard and most common usage of「前向き」.
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon5-34.why.1: (b) Incorrect. When asking someone to sit facing forward in a physical direction, use 「前を向いて座ってください」.
default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon5-34.why.2: (c) Incorrect. A wind blowing against you is called 「向かい風 (むかいかぜ)」, while a following wind is 「追い風 (おいかぜ)」; 「前向きな風」is not used.

default.q.n3-tango-t17-mon5-35.why.3: (d) Incorrect. To say that a room is tidied quickly or neatly, use 「さっと片付ける」 or 「すっきりと片付ける」, not 「あっさり」.

default.q.n3-tango-t18-mon1-1.why.0: (a) Correct. 指 has the on-reading し, and 導 has the on-reading どう; together they form 「指導」(しどう - guidance or instruction).

default.q.n3-tango-t18-mon1-2.why.0: (a) Correct. 開 has the on-reading かい and 店 has the on-reading てん, forming 「開店」(かいてん, “opening a store”).
default.q.n3-tango-t18-mon1-2.why.1: (b) Incorrect because it mistakes the on-reading かい of 開 for the voiced reading がい, which belongs to 外.

default.q.n3-tango-t18-mon1-3.why.0: (a) Correct. The on-reading よう of 容 combines with the on-reading し of 姿 to form「容姿」(ようし - appearance, looks).

default.q.n3-tango-t18-mon2-14.explanation:
- Translation of the sentence: An effort aimed at solving a problem.
- Vocabulary: 解決（かいけつ）means to resolve or settle something satisfactorily, such as a problem, difficulty, or dispute. Common expressions include「問題を解決する」(solve a problem) and「解決策」(solution; means of resolving a problem).

  + 結 means to connect or conclude, as in 結果「けっか」(result) and 結論「けつろん」(conclusion). It has the on-reading 「けつ」but refers to tying or an outcome, contrasting with 決's sense of resolving or settling.

default.q.n3-tango-t18-mon3-18.verdict: The correct answer is 1. 極めて (extremely).

default.q.n3-tango-t18-mon4-30.why.1: (b) 「すぐに」(immediately) conveys immediacy and urgency; it does not have the relaxed sense of signaling that the time is approaching, as「そろそろ」does.
default.q.n3-tango-t18-mon4-30.why.2: (c) 「やっと」(“at last”) expresses a result achieved after a long period of effort or tiring waiting.
default.q.n3-tango-t18-mon4-30.why.3: (d) 「ついに」(finally, at last) indicates the outcome after a long process and is often used with the past form.
default.q.n3-tango-t18-mon5-31.verdict: The correct answer is 1 (努力を積み重ねる。).
default.q.n3-tango-t18-mon5-31.explanation:
- Meaning: 積み重ねる（つみかさねる）: to accumulate, to pile up; used both literally for stacking objects and figuratively for accumulating experience, effort, or knowledge.
- Common collocations: 努力を積み重ねる (to accumulate effort), 経験を積み重ねる (to accumulate experience), 研究を積み重ねる (to build up research).
- Example: 毎日練習を積み重ねて、ついに優勝することができた。(By practicing day after day, I was finally able to win the championship.)
default.q.n3-tango-t18-mon5-31.why.0: (a) Correct because 「努力を積み重ねる」is a fixed collocation meaning “to make continuous efforts” or “to build up one’s efforts.”
default.q.n3-tango-t18-mon5-31.why.1: (b) Incorrect because it is unnatural in the context of cleaning. For organizing or tidying books and school materials, use 「整理する」or 「片付ける」.
default.q.n3-tango-t18-mon5-31.why.2: (c) Incorrect because saving money for shopping is expressed with 「お金を貯める」 (“save money”) or 「貯金する」, not 積み重ねる in this context.
default.q.n3-tango-t18-mon5-31.why.3: (d) Incorrect because people (人) are not the objects that can be “piled up” when talking; the word is completely inappropriate for the object.
default.q.n3-tango-t18-mon5-32.verdict: The correct answer is 1 (彼の意見に賛同する。).
default.q.n3-tango-t18-mon5-32.explanation:
- Meaning: 賛同（さんどう）: agreement, support, approval (of another person's opinion, viewpoint, policy, or proposal).
- Sino-Japanese character meanings: 賛 (to approve), 同 (same, together).
- Common patterns: ～に賛同する (to agree with ~), 賛同を得る (to gain support).
- Example: 多くの市民がその計画に賛同した。(Many citizens supported the plan.)
default.q.n3-tango-t18-mon5-32.why.0: (a) Correct because 「意見に賛同する」 is the standard expression for agreeing with or supporting someone's opinion or viewpoint.
default.q.n3-tango-t18-mon5-32.why.1: (b) Incorrect because 賛同 is used for people's opinions or policies; for a film, if you find it good or moving, use 「感動した」 or 「気に入った」.
default.q.n3-tango-t18-mon5-32.why.2: (c) Incorrect because weather (天気) is a natural phenomenon and cannot be used with 賛同 (to agree with).
default.q.n3-tango-t18-mon5-32.why.3: (d) Incorrect because a room (部屋) is a space or object, not an opinion or viewpoint, and using the particle を is also grammatically incorrect.
default.q.n3-tango-t18-mon5-33.verdict: The correct answer is 1 (新しいビジネスを展開する。).
default.q.n3-tango-t18-mon5-33.explanation:
- Meaning: 展開（てんかい）: to develop, expand in scale (a business or project), or development/progression (of a plot or match: ドラマの展開).
- Kanji: 展 (to unfold, develop), 開 (to open, begin).
- Common expressions: ビジネス／事業を展開する (to develop or expand a business), 議論を展開する (to develop an argument or discussion).
- Example: この会社は海外にも事業を展開している。(This company is expanding its business overseas as well.)
default.q.n3-tango-t18-mon5-33.why.0: (a) Correct because 「ビジネスを展開する」 is a standard fixed expression meaning “to develop or expand a new business operation.”
default.q.n3-tango-t18-mon5-33.why.1: (b) Incorrect because a vehicle (車) is a means of transportation and is not used with 展開; for driving a car, use 運転する.
default.q.n3-tango-t18-mon5-33.why.2: (c) Incorrect because a room (部屋) is not a plan or business that can be “implemented.” For a room, use 掃除する or 片付ける.
default.q.n3-tango-t18-mon5-33.why.3: (d) Incorrect because weather (天気) is a natural phenomenon, so 展開 cannot be used.
default.q.n3-tango-t18-mon5-34.verdict: The correct answer is 1 (彼は非常に責任感が強い。).
default.q.n3-tango-t18-mon5-34.explanation:
- Meaning: 責任感（せきにんかん - responsibility, sense of responsibility): a personal quality of being responsible.
- Kanji components: 責 (blame, responsibility), 任 (duty, undertake), 感 (feeling, sense).
- Common expressions: 責任感が強い (have a strong sense of responsibility), 責任感がある (be responsible), 責任感に欠ける (lack a sense of responsibility).
- Example: リーダーには強い責任感が求められる。(A leader is expected to have a strong sense of responsibility.)
default.q.n3-tango-t18-mon5-34.why.0: (a) Correct because 「責任感が強い」 is the standard collocation for describing someone with a very strong sense of responsibility.
default.q.n3-tango-t18-mon5-34.why.1: (b) Incorrect because 責任感 is a noun referring to a person's quality and cannot be used as an adjective modifying a room (部屋).
default.q.n3-tango-t18-mon5-34.why.2: (c) Incorrect because 責任感 cannot be used to describe or be attributed to the weather (天気).
default.q.n3-tango-t18-mon5-34.why.3: (d) Incorrect because a vehicle (車) is an object and cannot have a sense of responsibility (責任感).
default.q.n3-tango-t18-mon5-35.verdict: The correct answer is 1 (きっぱりと断る。).
default.q.n3-tango-t18-mon5-35.explanation:
- Meaning: きっぱり: (adverb) decisively, bluntly, clearly, without hesitation (usually expressing a clear attitude or decision).
- Common expressions: きっぱり（と）断る (refuse decisively), きっぱり（と）辞める (quit decisively), きっぱり諦める (give up once and for all).
- Example: 嫌なことはきっぱり断ったほうがいい。(It is better to firmly refuse things you do not like.)
default.q.n3-tango-t18-mon5-35.why.0: (a) Correct. 「きっぱり（と）断る」 is an extremely common fixed expression meaning “to refuse decisively / bluntly.”
default.q.n3-tango-t18-mon5-35.why.1: (b) Incorrect because きっぱり expresses a decisive attitude and is not used for eating; to say that someone eats heartily, use 「もりもり」 or 「しっかり」.
default.q.n3-tango-t18-mon5-35.why.2: (c) Incorrect because きっぱり is not used for running; "run fast" is expressed with 「速く」 or 「ぐんぐん」.
default.q.n3-tango-t18-mon5-35.why.3: (d) Incorrect because きっぱり is not used for sleeping; sleeping soundly is expressed as 「ぐっすり（寝る）」.
default.q.n3-tango-t19-mon1-1.verdict: The correct answer is 1. けつだんりょく.
default.q.n3-tango-t19-mon1-1.explanation:
- Sentence translation: 「彼の決断力には感服した。」 (I greatly admired his decisiveness.)
- Vocabulary:
  + 決断力 (けつだんりょく): decisiveness, the ability to make firm decisions.
  + 感服 (かんぷく): admiration, respect (感服する: to admire, be impressed by).

  + リーダーには素早い決断力が求められる。(A leader is expected to make quick decisions.)
default.q.n3-tango-t19-mon1-1.why.0: (a) Correct. 決 (on-reading: けつ) + 断 (on-reading: だん) + 力 (on-reading: りょく) combine to form 「けつだんりょく」, meaning “decisiveness” or “decision-making ability.”
default.q.n3-tango-t19-mon1-1.why.1: (b) Incorrect because when 力 functions as a suffix indicating ability or capacity (as in 行動力, 記憶力, 集中力...), it is read 「りょく」, not 「りき」.
default.q.n3-tango-t19-mon1-1.why.2: (c) Incorrect because the on-reading of 断 is 「だん」 (voiced), not 「たん」.
default.q.n3-tango-t19-mon1-1.why.3: (d) Incorrect because it mistakes the reading of 断 for 「たん」and the reading of 力 for 「りき」.
default.q.n3-tango-t19-mon1-2.verdict: The correct answer is 1. そなえる.
default.q.n3-tango-t19-mon1-2.explanation:
- Sentence translation: 「最新の設備を備える。」 (Be equipped with the latest facilities.)
- Vocabulary & kanji readings:
  + 備える - そなえる: equip, install, prepare in advance.
  + 設備 - せつび: equipment, facilities.
  + 最新 - さいしん: latest, state-of-the-art.
- Extended example:
  + 万一の事故に備えて保険に入る。(Take out insurance in preparation for any unforeseen accident.)
default.q.n3-tango-t19-mon1-2.why.0: (a) Correct. The verb 備える (BỊ) has the kun-reading 「そなえる」 and means to equip, prepare, or have available.
default.q.n3-tango-t19-mon1-2.why.1: (b) Incorrect. 「たくわえる」 is the reading of 蓄 in 蓄える, meaning “to store up” or “to accumulate” money, knowledge, and so on.
default.q.n3-tango-t19-mon1-2.why.2: (c) Incorrect. 「かかえる」 is the reading of 抱 in 抱える, meaning to hold in one's arms or to have/carry difficulties, debts, and so on.
default.q.n3-tango-t19-mon1-2.why.3: (d) Incorrect. 「おさえる」 is the reading of 押 in 押さえる (press or hold down), or 抑 in 抑える (restrain or control).
default.q.n3-tango-t19-mon1-3.verdict: The correct answer is 1. かんきゃく.
default.q.n3-tango-t19-mon1-3.explanation:
- Sentence translation: 「彼女の演技は観客を魅了した。」 (Her performance captivated the entire audience.)
- Vocabulary & kanji:
  + 観客 (かんきゃく): audience, spectators watching a performance or sporting event.
  + 演技 (えんぎ): acting, acting ability.
  + 魅了 (みりょう): to captivate, enchant, fascinate.
- Extended example:
  + コンサート会場は多くの観客で埋め尽くされた。(The concert venue was packed with a large audience.)
default.q.n3-tango-t19-mon1-3.why.0: (a) Correct. 観 (meaning “viewing,” on-reading かん) + 客 (meaning “guest,” on-reading きゃく) is read 「かんきゃく」 (audience).
default.q.n3-tango-t19-mon1-3.why.1: (b) Incorrect because 客 (customer/guest) is read as 「きゃく」; the choice 「かんかく」is easily confused with 感覚 (sensation) or 間隔 (interval).
default.q.n3-tango-t19-mon1-3.why.2: (c) Incorrect because the common on-reading of 観 is 「かん」, not the voiced reading 「がん」.
default.q.n3-tango-t19-mon1-3.why.3: (d) Incorrect because both 観 was misread as 「がん」 and 客 as 「かく」.
default.q.n3-tango-t19-mon1-4.verdict: The correct answer is 1. ゆうこう.
default.q.n3-tango-t19-mon1-4.explanation:
- Sentence translation: 「二国間の友好関係を深める。」 (To strengthen the friendly relationship between the two countries.)
- Vocabulary:
  + 友好 (ゆうこう): friendship, friendliness.
  + 二国間 (にこくかん): between two countries, bilateral.
  + 深める (ふかめる): to deepen, strengthen (a relationship, understanding, etc.).

  + 両国は友好条約を締結した。(The two countries signed a treaty of friendship.)
default.q.n3-tango-t19-mon1-4.why.0: (a) Correct. 友 (on-reading: ゆう) + 好 (on-reading: こう) is read as 「ゆうこう」, meaning friendship or friendliness. Both kanji have long vowels.
default.q.n3-tango-t19-mon1-4.why.1: (b) Incorrect because the on-reading of 友 is 「ゆう」, with the long vowel 「う」; 「ゆこう」is missing the long vowel.
default.q.n3-tango-t19-mon1-4.why.2: (c) Incorrect because the on-reading of 好 is 「こう」, not 「きょう」.
default.q.n3-tango-t19-mon1-4.why.3: (d) Incorrect because it omits the long vowel in 友 and misreads 好 as 「きょう」.
default.q.n3-tango-t19-mon1-5.verdict: The correct answer is 1. さんせい.
default.q.n3-tango-t19-mon1-5.explanation:
- Translation: 「彼の意見に大いに賛成する。」 (I strongly agree with his opinion.)
- Vocabulary and Sino-Japanese readings:
  + 賛成 - さんせい: agreement, approval.
  + 大いに - おおいに: greatly, very much.
  + 意見 - いけん: opinion.
- Additional example:
  + その提案には大賛成です。(I completely agree with that proposal.)
default.q.n3-tango-t19-mon1-5.why.0: (a) Correct. 賛 (on-reading: さん) + 成 (on-reading: せい) is read as 「さんせい」(agreement or approval).
default.q.n3-tango-t19-mon1-5.why.1: (b) Incorrect. 賛 is read 「さん」, not 「ぜん」; 「ぜんせい」 is the reading of 全盛 or 前世.
default.q.n3-tango-t19-mon1-5.why.2: (c) Incorrect because 成 is read 「せい」, not 「しょう」; 「さんしょう」 is the reading of 参照 or 賛賞.
default.q.n3-tango-t19-mon1-5.why.3: (d) Incorrect because both kanji were misread: 賛 as 「ぜん」 and 成 as 「しょう」, as in 全勝 (an undefeated victory).
default.q.n3-tango-t19-mon1-6.verdict: The correct answer is 1. たくみに.
default.q.n3-tango-t19-mon1-6.explanation:
- Sentence translation: 「彼女は巧みにピアノを弾く。」 (She plays the piano skillfully / expertly.)
- Vocabulary and kanji meaning:
  + 巧み (たくみ): skillful, ingenious, refined (巧みに: adverb meaning skillfully or expertly).
  + 弾く (ひく): to play, pluck, or strike a musical instrument such as a piano or guitar.
- Extended example:
  + 彼は巧みな話術で聴衆を引きつけた。(He captivated the audience with his skillful speaking.)
default.q.n3-tango-t19-mon1-6.why.0: (a) Correct. 巧 (skillful) has the kun-reading 「たくみ（に）」in the na-adjective/adverbial form, meaning skillfully or cleverly.
default.q.n3-tango-t19-mon1-6.why.1: (b) Incorrect. 「じょうずに」 is the reading of 上手（に）, meaning skillfully or well.
default.q.n3-tango-t19-mon1-6.why.2: (c) Incorrect. 「うわてに」 is the reading of 上手 (meaning being in a superior position or having the upper hand).

default.q.n3-tango-t19-mon1-7.verdict: The correct answer is 1. かいはつ.
default.q.n3-tango-t19-mon1-7.explanation:
- Translation: 「新薬の開発に成功した。」 (We succeeded in developing a new drug.)
- Vocabulary and Sino-Japanese readings:
  + 開発 (かいはつ): development, exploitation, research and development.
  + 新薬 (しんやく): new drug.
  + 成功 (せいこう): success (成功する: to succeed).
- Extended example:
  + 新しいスマートフォン向けアプリを開発する。(Develop a new app for smartphones.)
default.q.n3-tango-t19-mon1-7.why.0: (a) Correct. 開 (on-reading: かい) + 発 (on-reading: はつ) is read 「かいはつ」(development, exploitation).
default.q.n3-tango-t19-mon1-7.why.1: (b) In common modern words, 発 is read as 「はつ」. The reading 「ほつ」 appears only in a few old or Buddhist terms, such as 発起 (ほっき/ほつき) and 発露 (ほつろ).
default.q.n3-tango-t19-mon1-7.why.2: (c) Incorrect because 開 is read as 「かい」 with an unvoiced sound, not 「がい」 with a voiced sound.
default.q.n3-tango-t19-mon1-7.why.3: (d) Incorrect because both 開 was misread as 「がい」 and 発 as 「ほつ」.
default.q.n3-tango-t19-mon1-8.verdict: The correct answer is 1. しんらい.
default.q.n3-tango-t19-mon1-8.explanation:
- Sentence translation: 「彼の人柄は信頼できる。」 (His character is trustworthy.)
- Vocabulary and kanji readings:
  + 信頼 (しんらい): trust, confidence (信頼する/できる: trust, be trustworthy).
  + 人柄 (ひとがら): character, personality, personal qualities.
- Additional example:
  + 彼は上司からも部下からも厚く信頼されている。(He is deeply trusted by both his superiors and his subordinates.)
default.q.n3-tango-t19-mon1-8.why.0: (a) Correct. 信 (on-reading: しん) + 頼 (on-reading: らい) is read as 「しんらい」(trust or confidence).
default.q.n3-tango-t19-mon1-8.why.1: (b) Incorrect because 頼 has the on-reading 「らい」, not 「れい」; 「しんれい」 is the reading of 心霊 or 神霊.
default.q.n3-tango-t19-mon1-8.why.2: (c) Incorrect because 信 has the on-reading 「しん」, not the voiced reading 「じん」; 「じんらい」 is the reading of 迅雷.
default.q.n3-tango-t19-mon1-8.why.3: (d) Incorrect; it misreads 信 as 「じん」 and 頼 as 「れい」.
default.q.n3-tango-t19-mon2-9.verdict: The correct answer is 1. 経済 (economy).
default.q.n3-tango-t19-mon2-9.explanation:
Meaning of the sentence: As the economy develops, life becomes increasingly prosperous.
- 経済 (けいざい): the economy, economics.
- Easily confused kanji:
  + 経 (with the 糸 radical) differs from 軽 (with the 車 radical).
  + 済 (with the 氵 radical) differs from 剤 (with the 刂 radical, as in 薬剤 and 洗剤).
- Example: 日本の経済状況が回復しつつある。(Japan's economic situation is gradually recovering.)
default.q.n3-tango-t19-mon2-9.why.0: (a) 経済: The correct kanji, meaning the economy or economic activity.
default.q.n3-tango-t19-mon2-9.why.1: (b) 経剤: the second kanji is incorrect because 済 (with the water radical 氵) was confused with 剤 (with the knife radical 刂, as in 薬剤 and 洗剤).
default.q.n3-tango-t19-mon2-9.why.2: (c) 軽済: The first kanji is incorrect, confusing 経 (silk radical 糸) with 軽 (vehicle radical 車, meaning light).
default.q.n3-tango-t19-mon2-9.why.3: (d) 軽剤: Both kanji are incorrect; the water radical has been confused with the vehicle radical, and the water radical with the blade radical.
default.q.n3-tango-t19-mon2-10.verdict: The correct answer is 1. 意見.
default.q.n3-tango-t19-mon2-10.explanation:
Meaning of the sentence: Respect the other person's opinion.
- 意見 (いけん): opinion, viewpoint, personal thoughts.
- Related kanji:
  + 意: thoughts, intentions, as in 意味 (meaning), 意志 (will), and 意図 (intention).
  + 見: perception, viewpoint, as in 見解 (viewpoint) and 見物 (sightseeing).
- Distinction: 意 and 異 (as in 異文化 and 異常) are both read い, but have completely different meanings. 異見 means a dissenting opinion or remonstrance and is rarely used; the common word for an opinion or viewpoint is always 意見.
- Example: 会議で自分の意見をはっきりと述べた。(I clearly expressed my opinion at the meeting.)
default.q.n3-tango-t19-mon2-10.why.0: (a) 意見: The kanji are correct, and the word means a person's opinion, viewpoint, or perspective.
default.q.n3-tango-t19-mon2-10.why.1: (b) 意気: Incorrect because the second kanji is wrong; the word is written with 気, read as いき, and means willpower, morale, or fighting spirit.
default.q.n3-tango-t19-mon2-10.why.2: (c) 異見: The first kanji is incorrect because it confuses the homophonous い in 意 with 異, meaning different.
default.q.n3-tango-t19-mon2-10.why.3: (d) 異気: Both kanji are incorrect; combining 異 and 気 does not form a suitable word.
default.q.n3-tango-t19-mon2-11.verdict: The correct answer is 1. 自然 (nature).
default.q.n3-tango-t19-mon2-11.explanation:
Meaning: to be grateful for nature's blessings / gifts.
- 自然 (しぜん - nature, natural).
- Easily confused kanji:
  + 然 (ぜん: composed of 月/肉, 犬, and 灬) is used in 自然 (nature), 当然 (of course), and 全然 (completely/not at all).
  + 燃 (ねん: with the 火 radical on the left) refers to burning or setting something alight, as in 燃える (to burn) and 燃料 (fuel).
  + 自 (じ/し: oneself, self) differs from 始 (し: to begin), as in 開始 and 始まる.
- Example: 週末は自然豊かな山へハイキングに行く。(On weekends, I go hiking in mountains rich in nature.)
default.q.n3-tango-t19-mon2-11.why.0: (a) 自然: Correct kanji, referring to nature or the natural world.
default.q.n3-tango-t19-mon2-11.why.1: (b) 自燃: Incorrect because the second kanji confuses 然 with 燃, which has the 火 radical indicating burning, as in 燃料.
default.q.n3-tango-t19-mon2-11.why.2: (c) 始然: The first kanji is incorrect because the homophonous し of 始 (to begin) was confused with 自.
default.q.n3-tango-t19-mon2-11.why.3: (d) 始燃: Both kanji are incorrect, confusing 自 with 始 and 然 with 燃.
default.q.n3-tango-t19-mon2-12.verdict: The correct answer is 1. 協力 (cooperation).
default.q.n3-tango-t19-mon2-12.explanation:
Meaning of the sentence: Work together to solve the problem.
- 協力 (きょうりょく): cooperation, collaboration, working together (often used with 協力する / 協力して).
- Distinction:
  + 協力 (きょうりょく): cooperation or joint effort among several people.
  + 強力 (きょうりょく): a na-adjective meaning powerful, strong, or highly influential (e.g., 強力な接着剤: very strong adhesive; 強力な味方: powerful ally).
- Example: 皆で協力して部屋をきれいに掃除した。 (Everyone worked together to clean the room.)
default.q.n3-tango-t19-mon2-12.why.0: (a) 協力: Correct. These are the correct kanji, meaning cooperation or working together toward something (きょうりょくする).

default.q.n3-tango-t19-mon2-13.verdict: The correct answer is 1. 生活 (DAILY LIFE).

default.q.n3-tango-t19-mon2-13.why.0: (a) 生活: The correct kanji; it refers to daily life and one's way of living.
default.q.n3-tango-t19-mon2-13.why.1: (b) 生括: Incorrect character. The second character is confused with 括, which has the hand radical 扌, as in 一括 and 総括; the correct character is 活, with the water radical 氵.
default.q.n3-tango-t19-mon2-13.why.2: (c) 性活: Incorrect first kanji, caused by confusing the homophones せい of 性 with 生.

default.q.n3-tango-t19-mon3-15.verdict: The correct answer is 1. 大変な.
default.q.n3-tango-t19-mon3-15.explanation:

- **Kanji and related vocabulary**:
  - 大変: great, tremendous, extremely. In the pattern 「大変な + N」 referring to a person or thing, it modifies the noun to indicate an extraordinary or remarkable degree (e.g., 大変な努力家 - an exceptionally hardworking person, 大変な美人 - an extraordinarily beautiful woman, 大変な人出 - an enormous crowd).
  - 努力家 (どりょくか): a person who consistently works hard, a diligent person.

default.q.n3-tango-t19-mon3-15.why.0: (a) 大変な: Correct. 「大変な」can directly modify nouns describing a person’s notable character or qualities, such as 努力家 or 読書家, emphasizing the extraordinary degree of that character or ability.
default.q.n3-tango-t19-mon3-15.why.1: (b) 非常な: Incorrect. 「非常な」 usually modifies nouns describing conditions, difficult circumstances, or emotions, such as 非常な苦労, 非常な危険, and 非常時. It is rarely used directly before a noun referring to a person, such as 努力家; 非常に followed by an adjective or verb is more natural.
default.q.n3-tango-t19-mon3-15.why.2: (c) 過度な: Incorrect. It means “excessive” or “extreme,” usually with a negative or harmful nuance, as in 過度なストレス (“excessive stress”) and 過度な運動 (“excessive exercise”). It is not used to praise a hardworking person.
default.q.n3-tango-t19-mon3-15.why.3: (d) 重大な: Incorrect. It means “重大” or “serious” and is used for matters, responsibilities, and mistakes, such as 重大な問題, 重大なミス, and 重大な責任; it does not modify a person.
default.q.n3-tango-t19-mon3-16.verdict: The correct answer is 1. 急に.

default.q.n3-tango-t19-mon3-16.why.1: (b) 早急に: Incorrect. It is read as さっきゅうに or そうきゅうに (TẢO CẤP), meaning “urgently” or “promptly.” It is commonly used for actions people are asked to take, such as 早急に対応する (respond urgently).

default.q.n3-tango-t19-mon3-16.why.3: (d) 急速に: Incorrect. It is read きゅうそくに (急速), meaning "quickly, at a rapid rate"; it describes the progress or development of things and phenomena, as in 急速に発展する (develop rapidly).
default.q.n3-tango-t19-mon3-17.verdict: The correct answer is 1. 極めて.
default.q.n3-tango-t19-mon3-17.explanation:

default.q.n3-tango-t19-mon3-17.why.0: (a) 極めて: Correct. This formal adverb means “extremely” or “highly” and naturally and accurately modifies evaluative adjectives such as 重要だ, 困難だ, and 遺憾だ.
default.q.n3-tango-t19-mon3-17.why.1: (b) 極端に: Incorrect. It is read きょくたんに and means “extremely,” “excessively,” or “in an extreme manner,” involving an abnormal bias in one direction, as in 極端に偏る (be extremely biased) and 極端な例 (an extreme example).
default.q.n3-tango-t19-mon3-17.why.2: (c) 大いに: Incorrect. Read おおいに, it means “very much” or “to a great extent,” and commonly modifies verbs expressing feelings, support, or actions, such as 大いに賛成する (strongly agree) and 大いに楽しむ (enjoy to the fullest).
default.q.n3-tango-t19-mon3-17.why.3: (d) 大層: Incorrect. Pronounced たいそう, it means “very, exceedingly” and has an old-fashioned literary or colloquial nuance, which does not fit the formal, standard style of this sentence.
default.q.n3-tango-t19-mon3-18.verdict: The correct answer is 1. 確かに.

default.q.n3-tango-t19-mon3-23.why.2: (c) 非常に: Incorrect. It means “very, extremely” in a neutral, ordinary way. In the context of evaluating quality in formal exam language, 「極めて優れている」 is the most standard expression.

default.q.n3-tango-t19-mon4-26.verdict: The correct answer is 1. 落ち着いている (calm, composed).

default.q.n3-tango-t19-mon4-27.explanation:

default.q.n3-tango-t1-mon4-29.explanation:

default.q.n3-tango-t1-mon4-30.why.1: (b) 「すでに」(既に) means “already,” equivalent to もう. It is used for a completed event or an existing state, not merely for something beginning immediately.
default.q.n3-tango-t1-mon4-30.why.2: (c) 「さらに」(更に) means “further” or “in addition,” indicating an increase in degree; it does not express when an event takes place.
default.q.n3-tango-t1-mon4-30.why.3: (d) 「すぐに」(直ぐに) means “immediately, right away,” describing something that happens without any time delay, so it accurately replaces 「たちまち」.

default.q.n3-tango-t20-mon3-15.why.0: (a) 極めて: an adverb meaning “extremely, very,” used in formal or written language to modify an adjective or a noun describing a quality or characteristic (極めて優秀: extremely outstanding). It is highly appropriate for formally evaluating a person.

default.q.n3-tango-t20-mon3-15.why.2: (c) 大いに means “greatly” or “very much” and commonly modifies verbs expressing emotions, actions, or degree, such as 大いに楽しむ and 大いに期待する. It is rarely used to directly modify an adjective such as 優秀な.
default.q.n3-tango-t20-mon3-15.why.3: (d) 大層: Meaning 'very' or 'exceedingly,' it often has an old-fashioned, somewhat exaggerated, or sarcastic conversational nuance (for example, 大層なごちそう), so it is unsuitable for the formal commentary style here.

default.q.n3-tango-t20-mon3-22.explanation:
Meaning of the sentence: The business/project is expanding smoothly.
• Vocabulary and Sino-Japanese readings:
- 順調 (じゅんちょう): favorable, smooth, progressing as planned.
- 事業 (じぎょう): business, enterprise, project.
- 拡大 (かくだい): expansion, enlargement.
- 好調 (こうちょう): favorable condition, good performance.
- 順序 (じゅんじょ): order, sequence.
- 快調 (かいちょう): smooth, going well, in good form.
• Additional example:
手術後の回復は順調で、来週には退院できそうだ。(Recovery after the operation is progressing well, so I will probably be able to leave the hospital next week.)
default.q.n3-tango-t20-mon3-22.why.0: (a) 順調: A na-adjective meaning “smooth, favorable, on schedule.” The expression 「順調に〜」(for example, 順調に拡大している or 順調に進んでいる) correctly indicates that work is progressing smoothly without obstacles.
default.q.n3-tango-t20-mon3-22.why.1: (b) 好調 means being in good condition, performing well, or doing well in business (commonly used as 好調だ / 好調を保つ / 業績が好調), and is rarely used adverbially as 好調に拡大する, unlike 順調.
default.q.n3-tango-t20-mon3-22.why.2: (c) 順序 is a noun meaning “order” or “sequence,” as in 順序よく並ぶ; it is not an adjective modifying an action involving expansion in scale.
default.q.n3-tango-t20-mon3-22.why.3: (d) 快調 means “running smoothly” or “in excellent condition,” commonly used for machinery or an athlete’s physical condition, as in 車のエンジンが快調だ. It is not used to describe a company’s expanding scale.

However, grammatically, the question contains な, so answer 2 is not completely accurate (絶え間ない is an -i adjective and directly modifies a noun as in 絶え間ない努力; if the sentence contains な, the grammatically correct word is 1. 不断 (不断な努力)).
default.q.n3-tango-t20-mon3-23.explanation:
Sentence translation: She continued making efforts again and again without stopping.
• Grammar and answer notes:
- Strictly speaking, given the particle な in the prompt (___な努力), the na-adjective 不断 fits grammatically (不断な努力: unceasing effort).
- However, based on the provided answer choices (2. 絶え間ない), the very common expression 絶え間ない努力 is likely intended. The prompt may contain an extra な added during editing, since 絶え間ない is an i-adjective and directly modifies the noun without な.
• Vocabulary:
- 絶え間ない (たえまない): unceasing, continuous.
- 不断 (ふだん): uninterrupted, continuous, persistent.
- 努力を重ねる (どりょくをかさねる): to make continual efforts, to accumulate efforts.
- 無限 (むげん): infinite, limitless.
- 永遠 (えいえん): eternal, everlasting.
• Additional example:
絶え間ない努力の結果、彼女は見事に試験に合格した。 (As a result of her unceasing efforts, she passed the exam with flying colors.)
default.q.n3-tango-t20-mon3-23.why.0: (a) 不断: A noun / na-adjective meaning “unremitting, continuous” (FUDAN). The phrase 「不断な努力」(or 不断の努力) is a standard Sino-Japanese expression for persistent, uninterrupted effort.
default.q.n3-tango-t20-mon3-23.why.1: (b) 絶え間ない: An i-adjective meaning “unending, nonstop, continuous,” usually used directly before a noun: 絶え間ない努力. It does not require the particle な. If the test omits な, this is the most natural answer in modern Japanese.
default.q.n3-tango-t20-mon3-23.why.2: (c) 無限: means “infinite, without limits” (often used in 無限の可能性 - limitless potential, 無限の力 - infinite power), so it is not used to describe a process of effort over time.
default.q.n3-tango-t20-mon3-23.why.3: (d) 永遠: Means “eternal” or “forever” (commonly used in 永遠の愛 - eternal love and 永遠に続く - continue forever), so it is not used to modify 努力.
default.q.n3-tango-t20-mon3-24.verdict: The correct answer is 1. 安全 (safety).
default.q.n3-tango-t20-mon3-24.explanation:
Sentence meaning: Protect the safety of this area.
• Vocabulary & kanji readings:
- 安全 (あんぜん): safety; safe, free from danger.
- 守る (まもる): protect, safeguard.
- 地域 (ちいき): area, region, locality.
- 安心 (あんしん): peace of mind, reassurance.
- 安泰 (あんたい): peace and stability.
- 安定 (あんてい): stability.
• Additional example:
住民たちが協力してパトロールを行い、町の安全を守っている。(The residents are working together to patrol the town and protect its safety.)
default.q.n3-tango-t20-mon3-24.why.0: (a) 安全: Means “safety” (being protected from danger, accidents, and crime). 「地域の安全を守る」 (protect the safety of the area/community) is the most standard and commonly used expression.
default.q.n3-tango-t20-mon3-24.why.1: (b) 安心 means "peace of mind" or "reassurance," describing a psychological state free from worry (安心感). Expressions such as "安心を与える" (provide reassurance) or "地域の安心・安全" are common, but when used independently with 守る in this sentence, 安全 is the objective and more accurate word.
default.q.n3-tango-t20-mon3-24.why.2: (c) 安泰: Means “safe and secure” or “stable,” commonly used for a position, status, family, or country, as in 地位は安泰だ and 将来は安泰だ; it does not combine with 地域の〜を守る.
default.q.n3-tango-t20-mon3-24.why.3: (d) 安定: Means “stability” or “balance” (for example, 雇用が安定する—employment becomes stable; 物価の安定—price stability), and is not used in the context of protecting public order or area safety.
default.q.n3-tango-t20-mon3-25.verdict: The correct answer is 1. 期待 (expectation, anticipation).
default.q.n3-tango-t20-mon3-25.explanation:
Meaning: I have high hopes for his future.
• Vocabulary & Sino-Japanese terms:
- 期待 (きたい): expectations, hopes.
- 将来 (しょうらい): future.
- 大いに (おおいに): greatly, very much.
- 希望 (きぼう): hope, personal aspiration.
- 要望 (ようぼう): request, demand, proposal.
- 念願 (ねんがん): long-cherished wish.
• Additional example:
親は子供の成長と将来の活躍に大いに期待している。(Parents have high hopes for their children's growth and future success.)
default.q.n3-tango-t20-mon3-25.why.0: (a) 期待: Means “expectation, anticipation” regarding someone’s or something’s success or potential. It is used in the pattern “[object] に大いに期待する” (“to have high expectations for...” ).
default.q.n3-tango-t20-mon3-25.why.1: (b) 希望: Means “aspiration, personal wish” (often used in the structure “[content] を希望する,” for example, 入学を希望する), and is not used in the structure 〜に大いに希望している when referring to another person’s future.
default.q.n3-tango-t20-mon3-25.why.2: (c) 要望: means a “request” or “demand” made to another person or an organization (for example, 市民の要望に応える), not a psychological expectation about the future.
default.q.n3-tango-t20-mon3-25.why.3: (d) 念願: means a long-cherished wish or aspiration (a noun; for example, 念願のマイホーム—a long-dreamed-of home). It is not used as a verb in this context.
default.q.n3-tango-t20-mon4-26.verdict: The correct answer is 1. あわてずに.
default.q.n3-tango-t20-mon4-26.explanation:
- Meaning: 「彼はいつも冷静に対処する。」(He always handles things calmly.)
- Sino-Japanese terms & vocabulary:
  + 冷静 (れいせい): calm, composed, level-headed.
  + 対処 (たいしょ): deal with, cope with, resolve a problem.
  + 慌てる (あわてる): panic, become flustered -> あわてずに: without panicking, calmly.
- Additional example:
  + どんな緊急事態でも、冷静に（＝あわてずに）判断することが大切だ。(It is important to make calm judgments, without panicking, in any emergency.)
default.q.n3-tango-t20-mon4-26.why.0: (a) 「あわてずに」(without panicking; calmly) is synonymous with 「冷静に」(calmly; composedly). Replacing it in the sentence expresses always handling problems calmly, without becoming flustered.
default.q.n3-tango-t20-mon4-26.why.1: (b) 「いそいで」means hurriedly or urgently and refers to the speed of an action; it does not mean remaining calm mentally.
default.q.n3-tango-t20-mon4-26.why.2: (c) 「のんびりと」 means leisurely or relaxed and is not appropriate in a context involving coping with or solving a problem.
default.q.n3-tango-t20-mon4-26.why.3: (d) 「きびしく」means “strictly, harshly,” describing a firm or disciplined attitude, not calmness.
default.q.n3-tango-t20-mon4-27.verdict: The correct answer is 1. あぶなくない.
default.q.n3-tango-t20-mon4-27.explanation:
- Meaning: 「この道は安全だ。」(This road is safe.)
- Sino-Japanese vocabulary:
  + 安全 (AN TOÀN — あんぜん): safe, free from danger.
  + 危険 / 危ない (dangerous): dangerous → 危なくない: not dangerous.
- Extended example:
  + 夜でも街灯が多くて、この道は安全（＝あぶなくない）です。(This road is safe even at night because there are many streetlights.)
default.q.n3-tango-t20-mon4-27.why.0: (a) 「あぶなくない」, meaning “not dangerous,” is equivalent in meaning to 「安全だ」, meaning “safe.” Both describe a state without risk or danger.
default.q.n3-tango-t20-mon4-27.why.1: (b) 「あぶない」(dangerous) is the complete opposite of 「安全だ」.
default.q.n3-tango-t20-mon4-27.why.2: (c) 「こわい」(scary) describes a person’s feeling of fear; it does not mean “safe.”
default.q.n3-tango-t20-mon4-27.why.3: (d) 「くらい」(dark) refers only to a lack of light and is not synonymous with safety.
default.q.n3-tango-t20-mon4-28.verdict: The correct answer is 1. やさしい.
default.q.n3-tango-t20-mon4-28.explanation:
- Meaning: 「彼女は親切な先生だ。」(She is a kind teacher.)
- Kanji-based terms & vocabulary:
  + 親切 (しんせつ): kind, considerate, willingly helpful.
  + 優しい (やさしい): gentle, kind, tender.
- Extended example:
  + 道に迷ったとき、親切な（＝やさしい）人が案内してくれた。(When I got lost, a kind person showed me the way.)
default.q.n3-tango-t20-mon4-28.why.0: (a) 「やさしい」 (“kind, gentle, considerate”) is closest in meaning and nuance to 「親切な」 (“kind, helpful”) when describing a teacher’s character or attitude toward students.
default.q.n3-tango-t20-mon4-28.why.1: (b) 「きびしい」 (strict) has a meaning opposite to gentleness and kindness.
default.q.n3-tango-t20-mon4-28.why.2: (c) 「こわい」 means "frightening" and describes something fierce or fear-inducing; it is not synonymous with 「親切な」.
default.q.n3-tango-t20-mon4-28.why.3: (d) 「つめたい」 (cold, indifferent) is the antonym of 「親切な」.
default.q.n3-tango-t20-mon4-29.verdict: The correct answer is 1. けいかく.
default.q.n3-tango-t20-mon4-29.explanation:
- Meaning of the sentence: 「プランを実行する。」(Carry out the plan.)
- Kanji and vocabulary:
  + プラン (plan): plan, proposal.
  + 計画 (けいかく): a detailed plan that has been formulated.
  + 実行 (じっこう): to carry out, implement.
- Distinctions:
  + 計画 (plan): the most broadly used term; combined with 「実行する」, it forms the natural phrase 「計画を実行する」.
  + 企画 (project plan, proposal): often used for planning a new project or program (企画を立てる).
  + 予定 (intention, schedule): focuses more on a predetermined time or schedule.
- Additional example:
  + 来月の旅行のプラン（＝計画）を立てている。(I am making plans for next month's trip.)
default.q.n3-tango-t20-mon4-29.why.0: (a) 「けいかく」(計画) is the most direct and accurate native Japanese equivalent of the loanword 「プラン」(plan), and it combines naturally in 「計画を実行する」 (“carry out a plan”).
default.q.n3-tango-t20-mon4-29.why.1: (b) 「いけん」(意見) refers to a personal opinion or view, not a plan.
default.q.n3-tango-t20-mon4-29.why.2: (c) 「きかく」(企画: project, proposal) emphasizes developing an idea for a new project, commonly used in 「企画を立てる」. It is not directly equivalent to the English sense of “plan,” represented by 「計画」.
default.q.n3-tango-t20-mon4-29.why.3: (d) 「よてい」(予定—plan, schedule) refers to a schedule or planned timing and is not normally combined with「実行する」.
default.q.n3-tango-t20-mon4-30.verdict: The correct answer is 1. ただちに.
default.q.n3-tango-t20-mon4-30.explanation:
- Meaning: 「すぐに駆けつける。」(To rush over immediately.)
- On’yomi and vocabulary:
  + すぐに: immediately.
  + 直ちに (TRỰC — ただちに): immediately, at once (more formal and decisive than すぐに).
  + 駆けつける (KHU — かけつける): to rush to the scene or location of an incident.
- Additional example:
  + 事故の知らせを聞いて、警察がただちに（＝すぐに）現場に向かった。(After hearing about the accident, the police immediately headed to the scene.)
default.q.n3-tango-t20-mon4-30.why.0: (a) 「ただちに」 (直ちに, immediately) is completely synonymous with 「すぐに」 (immediately), describing an action carried out at once without delay.
default.q.n3-tango-t20-mon4-30.why.1: (b) 「ゆっくり」 means "slowly" or "at a leisurely pace," the opposite of the urgency expressed by 「すぐに」.
default.q.n3-tango-t20-mon4-30.why.2: (c) 「そろそろ」 means “soon” or “it is about time,” referring to an action that is about to occur; it does not mean “immediately.”
default.q.n3-tango-t20-mon4-30.why.3: (d) 「やっと」(finally) describes achieving a result after a long period of waiting or effort; it does not mean immediately.
default.q.n3-tango-t20-mon5-31.verdict: The correct answer is 1: 難関を突破する。
default.q.n3-tango-t20-mon5-31.explanation:
- 突破 (とっぱ): to overcome, break through, or surpass (a difficult exam, obstacle, record milestone, or encirclement).
- 難関 (なんかん): a difficult hurdle, major obstacle, or demanding exam.
- Common expressions: 難関を突破する (to overcome a difficult exam/obstacle), 100万人を突破する (to surpass the one-million mark), 記録を突破する (to break a record).
- Additional example: 厳しい予選を突破して、決勝に進出した。(We overcame the grueling qualifying round and advanced to the final.)
default.q.n3-tango-t20-mon5-31.why.0: (a) Correct. 「難関を突破する」 is a common fixed collocation meaning to overcome or break through a difficult examination, a formidable challenge, or a major obstacle.
default.q.n3-tango-t20-mon5-31.why.1: (b) Incorrect. For mountains and physical obstacles, use 「山を越える」(to cross a mountain) or 「山に登る」(to climb a mountain), not 「突破」.
default.q.n3-tango-t20-mon5-31.why.2: (c) Incorrect. 「突破」 is not used with vehicles; overtaking a car is 「車を追い越す」, while repairing a car is 「車を直す」.
default.q.n3-tango-t20-mon5-31.why.3: (d) Incorrect: 「突破」 is not used with a room; entering a room is 「部屋に入る」, while cleaning or tidying it is 「部屋を片付ける」.
default.q.n3-tango-t20-mon5-32.verdict: The correct answer is 1: 文化の継承に努める。
default.q.n3-tango-t20-mon5-32.explanation:
- 継承 (けいしょう): inherit, carry on (a tradition, culture, career, position, or property from a previous generation).
- 文化 (ぶんか), 努める (つとめる: make an effort, strive).
- Common expressions: 伝統を継承する (carry on a tradition), 王位を継承する (succeed to the throne), 財産を継承する (inherit property).
- Additional example: 若い世代に伝統工芸の技術を継承していくことが重要だ。(It is extremely important to pass traditional craft techniques on to younger generations.)
default.q.n3-tango-t20-mon5-32.why.0: (a) Correct. 「継承」 means inheriting or carrying on traditions, culture, property, or status from one generation to the next.
default.q.n3-tango-t20-mon5-32.why.1: (b) Incorrect because 「映画」 (movies) is not something passed down to later generations, so it cannot be used with 「継承」; for watching movies, use 「映画を見る」.
default.q.n3-tango-t20-mon5-32.why.2: (c) Incorrect. 「天気」 (weather) is a natural phenomenon and cannot be inherited.
default.q.n3-tango-t20-mon5-32.why.3: (d) Incorrect. 「部屋」(room) is not used with 「継承」. For inheriting a house or property, use 「財産を相続する」; for cleaning a room, use 「部屋を掃除する」.
default.q.n3-tango-t20-mon5-33.verdict: The correct answer is 1: 目標を完遂する。
default.q.n3-tango-t20-mon5-33.explanation:
- 完遂 (かんすい): complete fully, carry through to the end (a task, mission, plan, or goal).
- 目標 (もくひょう): goal, objective.

default.q.n3-tango-t20-mon5-33.why.0: (a) Correct. 「完遂」means to carry out a task, goal, or plan completely and see it through to the end.
default.q.n3-tango-t20-mon5-33.why.1: (b) Incorrect because 「車」 (car) is a physical object, not a task or goal to complete; driving a car is 「車を運転する」.
default.q.n3-tango-t20-mon5-33.why.2: (c) Incorrect: 「天気」 (weather) is a natural phenomenon and cannot be completed.
default.q.n3-tango-t20-mon5-33.why.3: (d) Incorrect. 「部屋」(room) is not a job or plan; “clean the room” is expressed as 「部屋を掃除する」.
default.q.n3-tango-t20-mon5-34.verdict: The correct answer is 1: 彼は非常に責任感が強い。
default.q.n3-tango-t20-mon5-34.explanation:
- 責任感 (TRÁCH NHIỆM CẢM - せきにんかん): sense of responsibility, awareness of responsibility.
- Common expressions: 責任感が強い (have a strong sense of responsibility), 責任感がない / 責任感に欠ける (lack a sense of responsibility), 責任感を持つ (have a sense of responsibility).
